title: keras_vision_model_ResNet50_test fails with weights='imagenet'
trigger: Compiling and executing ImageNet ResNet50 with real weights creates a VM function whose live reference-register ordinal exceeds 0x3F.
implemented_relation: A live VM reference retains an exclusive physical register slot until the allocator releases that exact register ordinal.
validity_obligation: Register release decodes the full ordinal range defined by the current integer or reference register bank.
root_cause: The release path retained masks from the earlier 8-bit register encoding after register numbers expanded to 16 bits.
physical_effect: The allocator reuses a physical reference-register slot whose prior value is still live, replacing one HAL reference with another reference type.
consequence: ResNet50 execution reaches hal.allocator.allocate.const with a hal.buffer in the register where a hal.allocator is required and fails with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
repair: Commit b0adcaf replaces the 0x3F and 0x7F release masks with kRefRegisterCount and kIntRegisterCount, matching the expanded register banks.
observed_decision: The release path retained masks from the earlier 8-bit register encoding after register numbers expanded to 16 bits.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit b0adcaf replaces the 0x3F and 0x7F release masks with kRefRegisterCount and kIntRegisterCount, matching the expanded register banks.
review_note: The landed commit explicitly states that it fixes 1660, identifies the stale masks after the uint8-to-uint16 expansion, changes the two release masks, and describes reuse while the displaced value remains live. The report's final diagnosis identifies VM register allocation and its runtime error exhibits the resulting reference-type replacement.

title: The input buffer of reduce_window is always initialed to zero
trigger: A reduce_window minimum carries scalar initial value 100 over an input containing positive values.
implemented_relation: Each physical result accumulator begins with the initial value carried by the logical reduce_window operation.
validity_obligation: Buffer initialization preserves the reduce_window init operand before window elements are combined.
root_cause: The lowering hard-coded zero as the result-buffer initializer instead of reading the operation's init operand.
physical_effect: The minimum reduction retains zero for every output window.
consequence: Both LLVM and Vulkan backends return an all-zero 2x2 tensor instead of values 1, 4, 13, and 16.
repair: PR 4911 extracts a constant init value or loads a dynamic init buffer, fills the result with that value, and adds constant and argument-backed initialization tests.
observed_decision: The lowering hard-coded zero as the result-buffer initializer instead of reading the operation's init operand.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 4911 extracts a constant init value or loads a dynamic init buffer, fills the result with that value, and adds constant and argument-backed initialization tests.
review_note: The issue identifies the hard-coded zero fill, and the linked patch replaces that fill with the exact init operand and adds reduce_window regressions.

title: Leaked buffers for unused inputs
trigger: A cross-module call returns one tensor reference while another input reference remains in the result register selected for replacement.
implemented_relation: Replacing a reference-register binding accounts for ownership of the displaced reference before installing the new reference.
validity_obligation: Reference-register replacement preserves the old identity until the VM reference operation can release or transfer it.
root_cause: The old result-pack variants zeroed opaque_ref, ref<T>, and optional<ref<T>> slots before managed assignment.
physical_effect: The displaced input buffer retains an unbalanced reference count.
consequence: The unused-input program leaves a buffer allocated at shutdown and Vulkan reports the outstanding allocation.
repair: Commit 15e51a85 removes the pre-assignment memset from reference result-pack variants and adds an unused-arguments regression.
observed_decision: The old result-pack variants zeroed opaque_ref, ref<T>, and optional<ref<T>> slots before managed assignment.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 15e51a85 removes the pre-assignment memset from reference result-pack variants and adds an unused-arguments regression.
review_note: The fixing patch changes the exact register-clearing operations implicated by the leak and includes the reported unused-input pattern.

title: [vulkan] Failed: Some allocations were not freed before destruction of this memory block
trigger: Benchmark iteration completes while the input VM list still owns HAL buffers allocated from the session device.
implemented_relation: All input-buffer references are released before the session and its device allocator are destroyed.
validity_obligation: Objects owning session-allocated buffers release those references before session teardown.
root_cause: iree-benchmark-module relied on scope destruction order that kept inputs alive beyond the session.
physical_effect: Vulkan Memory Allocator observes a nonempty allocation block during destruction.
consequence: The benchmark aborts with 'Some allocations were not freed before destruction of this memory block.'
repair: PR 3004 explicitly resets inputs before closing the session and adds the reported Vulkan benchmark command as a regression, later marked for the separate SwiftShader failure.
observed_decision: iree-benchmark-module relied on scope destruction order that kept inputs alive beyond the session.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 3004 explicitly resets inputs before closing the session and adds the reported Vulkan benchmark command as a regression, later marked for the separate SwiftShader failure.
review_note: Iteration capacity tracks the in-flight fence limit, the maintainer identifies retained inputs, and the linked fix adds inputs.reset immediately before session close.

title: Benchmark allocates buffers in each iteration without releasing after #4767
trigger: iree-benchmark-module repeatedly invokes a model whose result list contains reference values.
implemented_relation: Each returned reference has one owner in the result list and is released when that list is reset before the next invocation.
validity_obligation: VM list truncation releases owned references, and call transfer semantics move or retain each reference exactly once.
root_cause: The return calling convention and iree_vm_list_resize path did not implement matched ownership transfer and destruction for reference elements.
physical_effect: Device and host allocations accumulate across benchmark repetitions.
consequence: Repeated execution reaches VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY; reducing repetitions only delays it.
repair: PR 4858 implements reference-aware VM list resize/truncation, switches ref return handling to move semantics where appropriate, resets benchmark outputs, and adds resize tests for refs and variants.
observed_decision: The return calling convention and iree_vm_list_resize path did not implement matched ownership transfer and destruction for reference elements.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 4858 implements reference-aware VM list resize/truncation, switches ref return handling to move semantics where appropriate, resets benchmark outputs, and adds resize tests for refs and variants.
review_note: The allocation trace shows per-iteration retention, and the linked patch names #4852 while changing result ownership and adding reference truncation tests.

title: NVVM lowering assumes contiguous dense bindings, which is not always the case
trigger: A CUDA dispatch interface uses sparse or out-of-order binding identifiers, such as bindings 0, 4, and 7, instead of a dense sequence beginning at zero.
implemented_relation: The compiler and CUDA runtime translate each HAL binding identifier through the same sorted, compressed mapping to a dense kernel-argument position.
validity_obligation: Every participating layer uses one bijection from symbolic binding identifiers to dense kernel-argument positions; the mapping is independent of identifier density and descriptor enumeration order.
root_cause: The lowering and runtime equated a symbolic binding number with a dense array index without establishing that the binding set was dense and ordered.
physical_effect: The generated function or CUDA launch selected an absent or incorrect argument slot, which supplied the wrong device pointer or accessed storage outside the argument array.
consequence: The report records out-of-bounds accesses and heap corruption when bindings were not a dense ordered set.
repair: Commit 0dbd1ac collects binding identifiers, sorts them, and maps them to dense argument positions during lowering. The CUDA command buffer independently sorts descriptor bindings by identifier and writes their device pointers to consecutive argument slots. The compiler regression uses out-of-order sparse identifiers 4, 0, and 7 with distinct element types to check the resulting argument order.
observed_decision: The lowering and runtime equated a symbolic binding number with a dense array index without establishing that the binding set was dense and ordered.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 0dbd1ac collects binding identifiers, sorts them, and maps them to dense argument positions during lowering. The CUDA command buffer independently sorts descriptor bindings by identifier and writes their device pointers to consecutive argument slots. The compiler regression uses out-of-order sparse identifiers 4, 0, and 7 with distinct element types to check the resulting argument order.
review_note: Issue 5017 identifies the direct binding-number indexing assumption and its sparse-binding failure. GitHub connects the issue to merged PR 6044, and the issue closes at the PR's merge time. The landed commit names the dense-set assumption, changes both the compiler and CUDA runtime to the same sorted-and-compressed convention, and adds a compiler test whose sparse, out-of-order bindings expose the old mapping.

title: Sequence return types failing in the python bindings.
trigger: An exported function returns a tuple containing one or more scalar tensors.
implemented_relation: SIP result ordinal k selects VM output k and occupies Python sequence position k.
validity_obligation: ABI decoding uses the same zero-based result identity in SIP metadata, VM storage, and the Python sequence.
root_cause: The Python function ABI applied an off-by-one offset when retrieving result values.
physical_effect: Returned tensor handles bind to the wrong Python positions or no position.
consequence: Tuples such as (1,2,3) are returned as sequences containing None and missing values.
repair: PR 5347 corrects result retrieval to outputs->Get(ordinal), normalizes ABI sequences to tuples, and adds tuple lengths zero through three plus nested pytree tests.
observed_decision: The Python function ABI applied an off-by-one offset when retrieving result values.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 5347 corrects result retrieval to outputs->Get(ordinal), normalizes ABI sequences to tuples, and adds tuple lengths zero through three plus nested pytree tests.
review_note: The PR identifies an ABI off-by-one error, changes the output-list access by one index, and adds the report's tuple-arity cases.

title: OUT_OF_RANGE error in stateful program
trigger: One function stores the same value to two globals while another function stores only the first global.
implemented_relation: Globals share physical storage only when their store correlation is symmetric across every analyzed callable block.
validity_obligation: Fusion requires mutual, path-consistent correlation for every member of an equivalence class.
root_cause: One-way co-occurrence was accepted as an equivalence relation.
physical_effect: Later reads use offsets in a fused allocation whose logical contents no longer match the separate globals.
consequence: Stateful calls produce variable values and an out-of-range copy at offset 64 in a 48-byte buffer.
repair: PR 8008 intersects each candidate correlation set with every member's correlation set and clears candidates that are not self-correlated; it adds an asymmetric-store regression.
observed_decision: One-way co-occurrence was accepted as an equivalence relation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8008 intersects each candidate correlation set with every member's correlation set and clears candidates that are not self-correlated; it adds an asymmetric-store regression.
review_note: The issue's failing IR shows fused divergent globals, while the patch names issue 7988 and adds that exact asymmetric pattern as a test.

title: mhlo.gather to mhlo.select results in incorrect slice selected
trigger: A gather/select computation loads and stores tensor slices whose source view has nonzero offsets or non-unit strides.
implemented_relation: The load/store offsets and strides identify the physical source and destination regions represented by each tensor slice.
validity_obligation: A destructive-update rewrite preserves the physical region denoted by every source and destination slice.
root_cause: The rewrite constructed replacement slice operations without folding the load/store offsets and strides into their access descriptors.
physical_effect: The select reads a different section of the parent buffer from the section named by the source slice.
consequence: The two output rows are shifted to values from the preceding input rows instead of the expected slices.
repair: PR 8793 folds the dispatch load/store offsets and strides into the replacement extract_slice and insert_slice operations and adds offset, stride, and rank-reduction tests.
observed_decision: The rewrite constructed replacement slice operations without folding the load/store offsets and strides into their access descriptors.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8793 folds the dispatch load/store offsets and strides into the replacement extract_slice and insert_slice operations and adds offset, stride, and rank-reduction tests.
review_note: The issue isolates a wrong subregion, and the linked patch explicitly identifies omitted offsets and strides, restores them in both load and store rewrites, and adds regression coverage for those access descriptors.

title: Add a verification rule on HAL::EntryPointOp block to be non-empty.
trigger: A transform-interpreter pipeline applies workgroup-count construction through a pass nested under a special non-Module operation.
implemented_relation: Every executable entry point carries a populated workgroup-count region that deterministically maps its workload to a runtime dispatch grid.
validity_obligation: The workgroup-count transformation is applied directly to the executable variant and returns failure when it cannot populate the entry-point region.
root_cause: The pipeline treated successful pass-manager invocation as proof that a pass anchored on the special root had executed.
physical_effect: The runtime reaches a dispatch without a defined mapping from workload dimensions to workgroup counts.
consequence: The reported execution exhibits undefined, run-varying thread counts and flaky single-thread results.
repair: Commit 1b9e84c extracts setNumWorkgroupsImpl as a directly callable function, adds iree_set_num_workgroups_to_one to the transform dialect, invokes the implementation on the top-level HAL executable variant, and removes the unreliable nested pass path.
observed_decision: The pipeline treated successful pass-manager invocation as proof that a pass anchored on the special root had executed.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 1b9e84c extracts setNumWorkgroupsImpl as a directly callable function, adds iree_set_num_workgroups_to_one to the transform dialect, invokes the implementation on the top-level HAL executable variant, and removes the unreliable nested pass path.
review_note: The landed commit names bug 8823, explains that pass nesting on non-Module roots may do nothing without a report, replaces that path with a direct implementation call, and states that the old behavior produced flaky single-thread results.

title: Data race: `iree_task_worker_try_steal_task` vs `iree_task_executor_destroy`
trigger: Executor destruction overlaps a live worker's attempt to steal from another worker selected for teardown.
implemented_relation: Every worker and poller data structure remains valid until all threads that can access it have exited.
validity_obligation: Shutdown requests all exits, joins every worker and the poller, and only then deinitializes shared worker structures.
root_cause: Executor teardown combined join and deinitialization per worker instead of separating global thread exit from data-structure destruction.
physical_effect: A worker reads peer state concurrently with destruction of that state.
consequence: ThreadSanitizer reports a race between iree_task_worker_try_steal_task and iree_task_executor_destroy.
repair: PR 8873 splits request, await-exit, and deinitialize operations; the executor requests all exits, joins all workers and the poller, then deinitializes them.
observed_decision: Executor teardown combined join and deinitialization per worker instead of separating global thread exit from data-structure destruction.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8873 splits request, await-exit, and deinitialize operations; the executor requests all exits, joins all workers and the poller, then deinitializes them.
review_note: The report identifies peer stealing during destruction, and the merged patch explicitly separates global thread exit from worker and poller deinitialization.

title: Shutdown deadlock in `iree_task_worker_deinitialize` -> `iree_notification_await` as the thread is already gone
trigger: A worker reaches zombie state and posts its state notification after the waiting thread checks the condition but before that thread enters pthread_cond_timedwait.
implemented_relation: A notification wait either observes a satisfied condition or detects every notification posted after its wait token was captured.
validity_obligation: Prepare, condition check, and commit use a monotonic notification token so a post in the check-to-wait interval cancels the sleep.
root_cause: The pthread implementation signaled a condition variable but did not maintain the event-count epoch used by the notification contract.
physical_effect: The main thread waits indefinitely after the worker has exited and entered zombie state.
consequence: The dylib test intermittently hangs during iree_task_worker_deinitialize, roughly once per thousand repeated runs.
repair: PR 8877 gives the pthread path a mutex-protected epoch and waiter count; prepare snapshots the epoch, post increments it, and commit waits only while the epoch still equals the captured token.
observed_decision: The pthread implementation signaled a condition variable but did not maintain the event-count epoch used by the notification contract.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8877 gives the pthread path a mutex-protected epoch and waiter count; prepare snapshots the epoch, post increments it, and commit waits only while the epoch still equals the captured token.
review_note: The issue discussion derives the missed-post interleaving, the reporter validates the fix over repeated tests, and the merged PR states that it integrates the fix for this pthread deadlock.

title: `iree_hal_allocator_deallocate_buffer` segfault with minimal script
trigger: A Python function returns a device array after its local driver and device references leave scope.
implemented_relation: A HAL buffer stores the allocator used later to deallocate its storage.
validity_obligation: The backing allocator remains alive until every buffer that uses it has completed destruction.
root_cause: Buffer initialization stored the allocator pointer without retaining the allocator.
physical_effect: Later buffer destruction dereferences allocator state that has already been freed.
consequence: ASan reports a heap use-after-free and the minimal script segfaults during teardown across multiple drivers.
repair: Buffer initialization retains the device allocator, and buffer destruction releases it after deallocation.
observed_decision: Buffer initialization stored the allocator pointer without retaining the allocator.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Buffer initialization retains the device allocator, and buffer destruction releases it after deallocation.
review_note: The retain/release delta and regression test directly restore the lifetime relation identified in the issue.

title: Unsigned integer outputs become signed
trigger: An MHLO function accepts and returns a tensor<ui32>, and Python consumes the compiled result.
implemented_relation: The public function type carries logical unsignedness across signless internal arithmetic so the runtime result is decoded with the original dtype.
validity_obligation: Internal sign erasure does not erase signedness that remains observable at an external function boundary.
root_cause: The conversion target required signless integer types for func.func inputs, results, and returns instead of preserving the public unsigned boundary.
physical_effect: The exported element type identifies the result as generic INT_32, which the Python binding decodes as signed int32.
consequence: The reported sort computes correct bits but returns a signed array unless the result is manually bitcast to uint32.
repair: PR 13090 keeps unsigned types legal at public inputs and outputs and inserts explicit tensor.bitcast operations around the signless internal representation; it adds unsigned-boundary conversion tests.
observed_decision: The conversion target required signless integer types for func.func inputs, results, and returns instead of preserving the public unsigned boundary.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 13090 keeps unsigned types legal at public inputs and outputs and inserts explicit tensor.bitcast operations around the signless internal representation; it adds unsigned-boundary conversion tests.
review_note: The issue shows correct bits under bitcast, and the linked patch changes the exact boundary-type conversion while preserving signless internal tensors.

title: data race in `iree_hal_task_semaphore_multi_wait`
trigger: A worker resolves a task timepoint while the waiting thread begins cancellation cleanup.
implemented_relation: Cancellation uses a stable semaphore identity throughout asynchronous callback reset and waiter cleanup.
validity_obligation: The synchronization-object identity used by cleanup remains outside callback-cleared state until cleanup completes.
root_cause: The old waiter recovered the semaphore identity from the same base subobject that asynchronous resolution resets.
physical_effect: Worker memset and waiter pointer read race on base.semaphore.
consequence: ThreadSanitizer reports a data race in iree_hal_task_semaphore_multi_wait.
repair: Commit d83f4e46 stores a separate semaphore pointer in iree_hal_task_timepoint_t after acquisition and uses it for conditional cancellation.
observed_decision: The old waiter recovered the semaphore identity from the same base subobject that asynchronous resolution resets.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit d83f4e46 stores a separate semaphore pointer in iree_hal_task_timepoint_t after acquisition and uses it for conditional cancellation.
review_note: The archived TSan trace and fixing commit identify the same base.semaphore read/reset race and the repair introduces the proposed stable pointer.

title: IREE hardfaults on Arm bare-metal target when dispatching a 64bit op
trigger: ConstI64 dispatch reads a 64-bit immediate from a bytecode address without eight-byte alignment on Cortex-M.
implemented_relation: A bytecode operand is reconstructed with accesses permitted by the target for that operand width.
validity_obligation: Target policy distinguishes 64-bit alignment requirements from supported narrower unaligned accesses.
root_cause: One alignment flag represented every width and was also unconditionally reset in one configuration path.
physical_effect: The processor raises an alignment fault while decoding ConstI64.
consequence: IREE hardfaults when dispatching a function containing a 64-bit VM operation on Arm bare-metal targets.
repair: PR 9697 preserves an explicitly required alignment policy; PR 9705 adds IREE_MEMORY_ACCESS_ALIGNMENT_REQUIRED_64 and uses bytewise u64/f64 loads and stores on Arm while retaining native narrower accesses.
observed_decision: One alignment flag represented every width and was also unconditionally reset in one configuration path.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 9697 preserves an explicitly required alignment policy; PR 9705 adds IREE_MEMORY_ACCESS_ALIGNMENT_REQUIRED_64 and uses bytewise u64/f64 loads and stores on Arm while retaining native narrower accesses.
review_note: The issue pinpoints ConstI64's unaligned read, and PR 9705 states that it fixes 9593 by separating 64-bit Arm alignment.

title: rare shutdown deadlock in `executor_test`
trigger: The owner requests exit after the poller checks its state but before the poller resets and enters its wait.
implemented_relation: An exit request remains observable until the poller either consumes it or declines to block.
validity_obligation: The poller rechecks the exit state at the wait-commit boundary after any operation that can clear a concurrent wake signal.
root_cause: The old wait commit path could clear an exit wakeup and block without another state check.
physical_effect: The poller never reaches its zombie state and executor teardown waits indefinitely.
consequence: Approximately 0.5 percent of repeated executor tests deadlock during shutdown.
repair: PR 9724 adds a sequentially consistent EXITING check immediately before entering the system wait and returns when shutdown is pending.
observed_decision: The old wait commit path could clear an exit wakeup and block without another state check.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 9724 adds a sequentially consistent EXITING check immediately before entering the system wait and returns when shutdown is pending.
review_note: The PR description reconstructs the exact lost-wakeup interleaving, and the patch adds the state check at the wait boundary where that interleaving blocks.

title: Fix unaligned memory accesses

title: VUID-VkPipelineLayoutCreateInfo-pSetLayouts-00293(ERROR / SPEC) with Vulkan AMD 6900XT
trigger: A built-in Vulkan executable creates placeholder descriptor-set layouts for set numbers preceding its active storage-buffer set.
implemented_relation: Each pipeline set position refers either to the active bound resources or to an empty placeholder needed only to preserve set numbering.
validity_obligation: Placeholder set layouts preserve numbering without claiming active bindings or a second push-descriptor role.
root_cause: BuiltinExecutables created every placeholder with binding count one, and native layout creation enabled the push-descriptor flag independently of whether a set had real bindings.
physical_effect: VkPipelineLayoutCreateInfo contains more than one set layout marked VK_DESCRIPTOR_SET_LAYOUT_CREATE_PUSH_DESCRIPTOR_BIT_KHR.
consequence: Vulkan validation rejects the pipeline layout; on the reported AMD path no dispatch executes and dependent output is invalid.
repair: PR 10448 creates dummy layouts with zero bindings and enables the push-descriptor flag only when a layout contains at least one binding.
observed_decision: BuiltinExecutables created every placeholder with binding count one, and native layout creation enabled the push-descriptor flag independently of whether a set had real bindings.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 10448 creates dummy layouts with zero bindings and enables the push-descriptor flag only when a layout contains at least one binding.
review_note: The report's validation error names multiple push-descriptor sets, and the linked patch removes that state by making placeholder sets empty and conditioning the native flag on a nonzero binding count.

title: ASan failure in iree_task_list_erase
trigger: A wait retires while the poller still holds the task in its current traversal and wait list.

consequence: AddressSanitizer reports a stack-use-after-return in iree_task_list_erase.

title: Caching allocator causes wrong computation result
trigger: Repeated parameter updates acquire a free-pool buffer that still contains bytes from an earlier logical tensor.
implemented_relation: A reused physical buffer contains the requested logical tensor value before the allocator returns it to the caller.
validity_obligation: Reuse re-establishes the requested content relation in addition to capacity, usage, and ownership validity.
root_cause: The old caching allocator treated a matching reusable allocation as initialized even when initial_data was supplied.
physical_effect: Execution reads stale parameter bytes through a current logical binding.
consequence: Repeated set_params calls exchange parameter values and produce wrong numerical output.
repair: Commit 7be84611 writes initial_data into an existing buffer, checks the write status, and returns the buffer only after successful initialization.
observed_decision: The old caching allocator treated a matching reusable allocation as initialized even when initial_data was supplied.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 7be84611 writes initial_data into an existing buffer, checks the write status, and returns the buffer only after successful initialization.
review_note: The maintainer diagnosis, reporter retest, and exact fixing commit all identify the skipped existing-buffer initialization path.

title: mmt4d ukernel called with LHS pointer passed also for RHS and OUT
trigger: The VMVX mmt4d microkernel receives LHS, RHS, and output views whose HAL binding subspans use offsets 0, 256, and 512.
implemented_relation: A binding number and byte offset jointly identify the physical subspan passed to each microkernel argument.
validity_obligation: Lowering a binding subspan preserves both its binding identity and byte offset in the descriptor consumed by the microkernel.
root_cause: The memref representation treated a nonzero binding-subspan offset as if the memref began at offset zero on a backend without pointer-arithmetic lowering.
physical_effect: Pointer extraction collapses distinct subspans onto the same base address.
consequence: mmt4d is called with the LHS pointer for RHS and output, causing the matmul tests to fail.

trigger: One producer feeds multiple tilable consumers after consumer fusion creates additional producer opportunities.
implemented_relation: A fused producer value is yielded from a tiled loop only when one compatible consumer can receive that replacement.
validity_obligation: Yield selection accounts for the number and compatibility of tilable consumers and revisits producer opportunities after consumer fusion.
root_cause: TileDispatchUsingForall yielded a replacement for a value with multiple tilable consumers.
physical_effect: Part of the dispatch remains undistributed and executes with an incorrect workgroup-to-tensor mapping.
consequence: The LLVMGPU softmax dispatch returns incorrect numerical results.
repair: PR 19212 declines yielded replacement when a fused value has multiple tilable consumers, queues fusion work, and performs another producer-fusion pass with a softmax-shaped regression.
observed_decision: TileDispatchUsingForall yielded a replacement for a value with multiple tilable consumers.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 19212 declines yielded replacement when a fused value has multiple tilable consumers, queues fusion work, and performs another producer-fusion pass with a softmax-shaped regression.
review_note: The report's multi-use softmax IR is named as resolved by PR 19212, whose regression uses the same dimensions and whose guard targets multi-consumer yielded values.

title: PJRT plugin fails to execute in JAX while multiple GPUs are provided
trigger: JAX compiles a single-shard computation while the PJRT client exposes four addressable GPUs.
implemented_relation: A loaded executable's device list matches the device assignment selected for that compilation.
validity_obligation: Compilation preserves the selected device assignment in the loaded executable's execution-device list.
root_cause: PJRT_Client_Compile discarded its compile-options device assignment and unconditionally attached addressable_devices_.
physical_effect: JAX derives a four-shard execution requirement from an executable compiled for one assigned device.
consequence: execute_sharded_on_local_devices rejects one argument shard because it expects four.
repair: PR 19369 parses CompileOptionsProto, reads executable_build_options.device_assignment, selects those addressable devices, and passes that list to LoadedExecutableInstance.
observed_decision: PJRT_Client_Compile discarded its compile-options device assignment and unconditionally attached addressable_devices_.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 19369 parses CompileOptionsProto, reads executable_build_options.device_assignment, selects those addressable devices, and passes that list to LoadedExecutableInstance.

title: `scf.for` loop with zero-sized tensor hangs on `local-task` device but works on `local-sync`

title: GPU data races as LLVMGPUDistribute has ops distributed to multiple threads performing the same memory accesses
trigger: Kernel configuration selects LLVMGPUDistribute and a multi-thread workgroup for LinalgExt SortOp.
implemented_relation: The selected lowering pipeline binds one logical sort operation to a workgroup execution configuration.
validity_obligation: A multi-thread execution mapping assigns nonconflicting work or introduces synchronization sufficient for shared accesses.

observed_decision: The kernel configuration selected LLVMGPUDistribute for SortOp although that path did not distribute the operation.
