title: [GPU] very poor numerics for certain conv layouts
trigger: A convolution uses input and filter layouts whose shared reduction dimensions appear in different orders, such as HWC input and CHW filter order.
implemented_relation: Corresponding input and filter reduction dimensions must occupy the same positions in the flattened matrix-multiplication K dimension.
validity_obligation: Convolution lowering preserves the one-to-one correspondence and order of input and filter reduction coordinates in the flattened K dimension.
root_cause: The im2col representation recorded positions and strides but omitted the permutation from input shared-dimension order to filter shared-dimension order.
physical_effect: Each flattened input element is multiplied by a filter element from a different logical reduction coordinate.
consequence: The reported one-dimensional convolution returns 3 and 4 where the corresponding correct values are 5 and 6; CPU lowering remains correct.
repair: PR 20531 adds and verifies input_filter_perm, derives it from the two indexing maps, and applies it when constructing the im2col K basis; tests include the reported NHC/CHF permutation.
observed_decision: The im2col representation recorded positions and strides but omitted the permutation from input shared-dimension order to filter shared-dimension order.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 20531 adds and verifies input_filter_perm, derives it from the two indexing maps, and applies it when constructing the im2col K basis; tests include the reported NHC/CHF permutation.
review_note: The issue isolates a swapped reduction-coordinate order, and the patch derives, stores, validates, and consumes exactly that missing permutation while adding the reported layout as a regression case.

title: [dlpack][runtime] Memory leak with dlpack capsules
trigger: [dlpack][runtime] Memory leak with dlpack capsules
physical_effect: A misspelled DLPack capsule-consumption name breaks the ownership-handoff convention and prevents the external tensor deleter from reclaiming imported allocations.
consequence: Repeated Torch-to-IREE imports retain GPU allocations until the process exhausts device memory.
observed_decision: The import path renames a consumed capsule to a name other than the protocol-defined used_dltensor marker, so capsule destruction follows the wrong ownership state.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Renaming the capsule according to the protocol removes the leak; maintainers identify the typo, find the leak, confirm the reproducer no longer leaks, and close the issue.
review_note: The discussion reports that a capsule-name typo was fixed and PR 893 removes a workaround after an IREE version bump, but the underlying runtime patch is absent; the repair site and exact source delta cannot be verified.

title: [Flux] Empty output from the flux models
trigger: Shortfin loads a VMFB compiled by an older IREE compiler into a runtime that no longer consumes block_shared_memory_size.
implemented_relation: A compiled kernel export records the dynamic shared-memory amount that its matching runtime must either honor or reject as incompatible.
validity_obligation: Compiler and runtime agree on launch-resource fields, or the loader rejects an artifact whose nonzero requirement it cannot honor.
root_cause: The runtime deprecated and ignored the field without rejecting older artifacts that still carried a nonzero value.
physical_effect: The HIP launch provides no dynamically allocated shared memory to a kernel compiled to use it.
consequence: Flux execution completes with empty or garbage output instead of raising a compatibility error.
repair: PR 21118 restores access to the serialized field and rejects any nonzero value with a compiler/runtime-version diagnostic.
observed_decision: The runtime deprecated and ignored the field without rejecting older artifacts that still carried a nonzero value.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 21118 restores access to the serialized field and rejects any nonzero value with a compiler/runtime-version diagnostic.
review_note: The issue's size comparison identifies a stale VMFB, and the patch explicitly prevents silent execution of precisely that nonzero legacy field.

title: Wrong result due to resource reuse in stream dialect
trigger: Wrong result due to resource reuse in stream dialect
physical_effect: Two sequential bidirectional-LSTM loops are assigned subviews of the same transient resource, allowing the backward computation to overwrite the forward result before both outputs are consumed.
consequence: The forward-direction columns are replaced by the reversed backward result, yielding a reproducible incorrect tensor.
observed_decision: Stream resource planning passes the first loop's resource subviews into the second loop instead of allocating an independent resource for the second live value.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The report provides full phase IR and a controlled stream-level edit that duplicates the resource; recompiling that edit restores the expected output.
review_note: A controlled IR edit restores output, but no repository repair, maintainer adjudication, or fixed regression connects that edit to an implemented correction.

title: Getting non-deterministic inf, -inf, and nan's with optimized Wave kernel
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iREE Wave-generated buffer loads for tensors imported from parameter archives with nonzero physical offsets.
physical_effect: Loads address unrelated bytes from the imported allocation.
consequence: Optimized execution produces nondeterministic infinities and NaNs.
observed_decision: The optimized kernel uses stream.binding.subspan from offset zero rather than extracting the actual strided metadata offset.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The reporter suggests memref.extract_strided_metadata to carry the actual offset.
review_note: No linked patch, maintainer adjudication, or fixed regression establishes the proposed repair.

title: There is an issue with the circular buffer in hip_device.c
trigger: A parameter file larger than the staging buffer is uploaded in multiple chunks while earlier upload work remains active.
implemented_relation: Each in-flight file range retains a distinct staging-buffer region until the queued HIP transfer has consumed that region.
validity_obligation: A staging-buffer region is not reused until every transfer reading that region has completed.
root_cause: The circular upload path admitted continued reuse without establishing region-specific completion for the bytes selected next.
physical_effect: Bytes used by queued parameter transfers can be replaced by later file chunks.
consequence: Very large models receive corrupted parameters and exhibit nondeterministic execution.
repair: PR 21758 changes admission from enough free bytes for one chunk to the entire transfer buffer being free, disabling overlapping circular-buffer reuse.
observed_decision: The circular upload path admitted continued reuse without establishing region-specific completion for the bytes selected next.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 21758 changes admission from enough free bytes for one chunk to the entire transfer buffer being free, disabling overlapping circular-buffer reuse.
review_note: The issue and merged change both attribute large-model parameter corruption to circular upload behavior; the change serializes reuse by waiting for the full buffer to become free.

title: [iree-run-module] Issues in using --expected_output flag for si64 type
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iree-run-module comparison of signless integer results against signed NPY expected-output files.
physical_effect: Expected and actual buffers with compatible bits are rejected or can be conflated under ambiguous signedness.
consequence: The --expected_output check fails for si64/signless i64 combinations.
observed_decision: The tooling cannot represent signless integers in NPY and its comparison path does not have an explicit user-supplied type binding.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24804 proposes an explicit policy; a downstream CI comparison change does not repair IREE tooling.
review_note: PR 24804 was not merged, and discussion has not selected and landed a comparison contract with regression coverage.

title: Unwanted removal of LDS memory reads when using subgroup specialization
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iREE vector-transfer optimization of LDS reads under subgroup specialization.
physical_effect: Consumer subgroups lose the cross-subgroup LDS values required inside the loop.
consequence: The generated optimized Wave kernel returns incorrect data.
observed_decision: The pass reasons locally about a subgroup that does not write a shared-memory value and moves or removes reads whose producer belongs to another subgroup.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The report supplies before/after IR and identifies the moved reads.
review_note: No correcting dependence analysis, landed patch, or fixed regression is linked.

title: [Runtime] float64 operations produce corrupted output (buffer size mismatch)
trigger: [Runtime] float64 operations produce corrupted output (buffer size mismatch)
physical_effect: F64 demotion keeps the public ABI typed as f64 while representing the function body as f32 and bridges them with a bitcast whose source and destination have different total byte sizes.
consequence: HAL allocates 16 bytes for four f64 values that require 32 bytes, so the tail is dropped and Python observes truncated or corrupted results.
observed_decision: DemoteF64ToF32Pass emits hal.tensor import/export with f64 encoding and f32 storage, while the compatibility verifier permits the size-changing bitcast.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The report compares unaffected types; the follow-up traces the mismatch through post-pass and final HAL IR and specifies explicit truncation/extension plus verifier checks as the repair.
review_note: The report proposes explicit conversion and verifier checks, but no implemented patch or fixed-version execution demonstrates the repair.

title: `hoistOneStaticallyBoundAllocation` produces bogus 2^52-element static `alloca`s when dynamic dim bounds default to the `index` umax
trigger: A dynamic dimension carrying the default index upper bound is transformed by ceildiv and used to size a CPU intermediate alloca.
implemented_relation: Every stack allocation admitted to LLVM has a finite byte size computed without arithmetic overflow and within the configured stack limit.
validity_obligation: Allocation-size products, alignment, and cumulative totals either remain exact and within the limit or stop compilation with a diagnostic.
root_cause: LLVMCPUCheckIRBeforeLLVMConversion accepted a wrapped allocation size as a valid bounded stack allocation.
physical_effect: Generated loads and stores derive from an llvm.alloca poison pointer rather than storage for the logical intermediate tensor.
consequence: Dynamic inner-tiled CPU models compile without a diagnostic and can silently lose accumulator values or return otherwise incorrect results.
repair: PR 24745 computes shaped sizes, dynamic-bound products, alignment, and cumulative allocation totals with 64-bit overflow checks and emits an error when any calculation overflows.
observed_decision: LLVMCPUCheckIRBeforeLLVMConversion accepted a wrapped allocation size as a valid bounded stack allocation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24745 computes shaped sizes, dynamic-bound products, alignment, and cumulative allocation totals with 64-bit overflow checks and emits an error when any calculation overflows.
review_note: The merged patch describes the report's default-bound allocation, poison-pointer lowering, and silent wrong-result reproducer, then changes and tests the exact resource check that admitted it.

title: [CUDA] Runtime export lookup uses unsanitized name while compilation sanitizes export names
trigger: Compilation creates a CUDA dispatch named `callee$async_dispatch_0_elementwise_4_f32` and sanitizes the PTX kernel symbol while the runtime later looks up the original export name.
implemented_relation: Each logical IREE export identity maps to one backend-valid PTX kernel symbol, with both names retained for their respective consumers.
validity_obligation: Backend symbol sanitization changes only the physical kernel identifier; it preserves an explicit mapping from the unchanged logical export name to that identifier.
root_cause: CUDA serialization reused the sanitized backend symbol as the logical export identity, collapsing two names with different naming rules into one field.
physical_effect: The runtime's direct export-name comparison could not resolve the requested function even though the compiled PTX kernel was present.
consequence: iree-run-module failed with `NOT_FOUND; function 'callee$async_dispatch_0_elementwise_4_f32' not found in executable`, while the CPU backend ran the same module.
repair: PR 24889 appends an optional export_name field to the CUDA executable schema, serializes the original IREE name there, keeps the sanitized kernel_name for cuModuleGetFunction, and stores export_name in the runtime lookup table. New runtimes fall back to kernel_name for older VMFBs.
observed_decision: CUDA serialization reused the sanitized backend symbol as the logical export identity, collapsing two names with different naming rules into one field.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24889 appends an optional export_name field to the CUDA executable schema, serializes the original IREE name there, keeps the sanitized kernel_name for cuModuleGetFunction, and stores export_name in the runtime lookup table. New runtimes fall back to kernel_name for older VMFBs.
review_note: The issue identifies the compiler sanitization and runtime equality check and supplies a `$`-containing reproducer. The first proposed repair, PR 24718, was closed by an IREE maintainer as addressed by PR 24889. The merged PR describes the same lookup failure, separates the original export name from the PTX symbol, and reports that its CUDA reproduction succeeds after the change.

title: [LinalgExt] Sort op causes incorrect bufferization
trigger: [LinalgExt] Sort op causes incorrect bufferization
physical_effect: Bufferization performs destructive destination-style sort and scatter updates directly in an input tensor's storage even though the original SSA tensor remains live and is returned separately.
consequence: Sorting or scattering mutates both the operation result and the separately returned input, causing downstream calculations to consume reordered values and return incorrect tensors.
observed_decision: The bufferizer assigns the operation result and its outs operand the same resource without inserting the copy needed to preserve the still-live pre-operation value.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Two minimized programs contrast the faulty LinalgExt behavior with linalg.generic, and stream IR shows multiple logically distinct values mapped to the same transient range.
review_note: The report shows destructive bufferization and its consequence, but no source-localized repair or fixed regression is available.

title: [Codegen][LLVMCPU] Un-hoisted in-loop stack alloca in the matmul overflows the worker stack
trigger: A large data-tiled matmul is compiled with distribution disabled, leaving loadProcessorData in the inner loop.
implemented_relation: A temporary processor-data slot has function lifetime and consumes one bounded stack allocation, while per-call feature updates remain adjacent to the microkernel call.
validity_obligation: Function-lifetime scratch storage is allocated once outside loops, and loop-local code performs only bounded updates.
root_cause: DispatchABI constructed the processor-data allocation at the caller's current insertion point without separating storage reservation from per-call feature patching.
physical_effect: Stack consumption grows linearly with the matmul tile count.
consequence: Large matmuls overflow the worker stack and crash, while small matrices complete.
repair: PR 24749 moves construction to the function entry block. PR 24786 refines the change: only the alloca is hoisted, while feature-bit stores remain at the call site so inlined microkernel checks still devirtualize. Both include IR checks for loop placement.
observed_decision: DispatchABI constructed the processor-data allocation at the caller's current insertion point without separating storage reservation from per-call feature patching.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24749 moves construction to the function entry block. PR 24786 refines the change: only the alloca is hoisted, while feature-bit stores remain at the call site so inlined microkernel checks still devirtualize. Both include IR checks for loop placement.
review_note: The report identifies the loop-local alloca; both linked merged patches name #24744, and the refinement explicitly separates the stack-allocation cause from feature-bit stores needed for devirtualization.

title: `hal.command_buffer.dispatch` OUT_OF_RANGE on 3.12.0rc but works on 3.11.0
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iREE VM branch-remap ownership for references passed to hal.command_buffer.dispatch under Python 3.12.
physical_effect: The live reference reaching the HAL call is missing or invalid.
consequence: Execution fails with OUT_OF_RANGE on Python 3.12 but succeeds on 3.11.
observed_decision: A branch remap applies an incorrect retain/release treatment to a reference consumed by the dispatch path.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24781 proposes fixing reference ownership in branch remaps.
review_note: PR 24781 was not merged, leaving no landed ownership repair or fixed regression.

title: [Vulkan] unaligned buffer transfer hangs
trigger: A small host buffer produces an unaligned Vulkan update that cannot use the native transfer instruction.
implemented_relation: The selected Vulkan queue supports every command used by the concrete aligned or emulated transfer path.
validity_obligation: Queue capability selection includes compute for transfer operations that may take the unaligned emulation path.
root_cause: The old logical-device code selected the queue from the abstract transfer category without the concrete replay path's compute requirement.
physical_effect: Vulkan rejects or drops the invalid command while a signal semaphore remains unsatisfied.
consequence: Validation reports errors and the host-to-device transfer hangs indefinitely.
repair: PR 24838 requires both transfer and compute flags for fill/update selection and retries with any affinity when the requested lanes cannot satisfy them.
observed_decision: The old logical-device code selected the queue from the abstract transfer category without the concrete replay path's compute requirement.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 24838 requires both transfer and compute flags for fill/update selection and retries with any affinity when the requested lanes cannot satisfy them.
review_note: The patch names unaligned fill/update replay and explains the exact transfer-only queue hang reported by issue 24771.

title: [Vulkan] mismatch between memory type selection heuristics
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iREE Vulkan memory-type selection consistency between direct allocation and pool-selection heuristics.
physical_effect: A request can be assigned to a pool whose memory properties differ from the direct allocator's selected type.
consequence: The report observes mismatched allocation behavior for the same compatibility set.
observed_decision: Two selection paths break equal-score memory-type ties differently.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PRs 24798 and 24799 propose aligning the tie-break order.
review_note: Both proposals were closed without merge, and no alternative landed change or regression is linked.

title: [Stream] SplitParameterEncoding in consolidate mode doesn't work
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises iREE Stream SplitParameterEncoding in consolidate mode.
physical_effect: Generated consolidated parameter references bind logical slices to incorrect physical segments.
consequence: The reported compilation path fails or produces invalid parameter access.
observed_decision: The pass's consolidation logic does not preserve all parameter ranges/encodings when splitting resources.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Maintainer discussion states that the pass requires a broader rework.
review_note: No implemented rework, landed patch, or fixed regression is available.

title: Sticking an array to it's own device does not work
trigger: An array resides uncommitted on GPU 0, the program explicitly applies device_put(array, GPU 0), then combines it with an array committed to GPU 1.
implemented_relation: An explicit device_put binds the result logically to its requested device even when its buffer already resides there.
validity_obligation: A physical no-copy decision preserves the bytes while still applying the requested logical commitment transition.
root_cause: _copy_device_array_to_device treated matching physical locations as proof that no state change was required and skipped the _device update.
physical_effect: When combined with a GPU 1 committed array, the supposedly GPU 0 committed operand is treated as movable and follows the GPU 1 operand.
consequence: The mixed-device addition executes on GPU 1 instead of raising the expected colocation error for operands committed to GPU 0 and GPU 1.
repair: Commit d315564 distinguishes physical residency from commitment: when the buffer already resides on the requested device but x._device differs, it reuses the buffer and constructs the result with the requested device commitment. It also re-enables the same-device commitment assertion.
observed_decision: _copy_device_array_to_device treated matching physical locations as proof that no state change was required and skipped the _device update.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit d315564 distinguishes physical residency from commitment: when the buffer already resides on the requested device but x._device differs, it reuses the buffer and constructs the result with the requested device commitment. It also re-enables the same-device commitment assertion.
review_note: A maintainer verifies the report's expected behavior after the placement work around PR 2882. The immediately following landed commit d315564 states the report's exact same-device device_put failure, changes that branch, and restores the corresponding commitment test.

title: `np.stack` does not respect stickied arrays
trigger: jnp.stack expands dimensions on an array committed to CPU and an uncommitted array resident on the default GPU.
implemented_relation: Lazy view operations preserve both the source buffer's physical device and its explicit device commitment.
validity_obligation: A metadata-only shape or axis transformation retains the placement commitment of the unchanged underlying buffer.
root_cause: The lazy broadcast, reshape, and transpose constructors copied the buffer but discarded operand._device.
physical_effect: The committed CPU operand is treated as movable and stack transfers or executes on the default GPU.
consequence: jnp.stack returns a GPU array although addition and concatenate over the same explicitly placed input follow CPU.
repair: Commit ac023bf passes operand._device into each lazy DeviceArray view constructor and adds placement tests distinguishing physical residence from commitment.
observed_decision: The lazy broadcast, reshape, and transpose constructors copied the buffer but discarded operand._device.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit ac023bf passes operand._device into each lazy DeviceArray view constructor and adds placement tests distinguishing physical residence from commitment.
review_note: The issue traces stack to singleton reshape losing the DeviceArray device field; the maintainer states PR 2882 covers it, and the merged patch changes that exact constructor and its placement tests.

title: Ops involving only CPU tensors run on device, not CPU
trigger: Indexing or reducing a CPU-backed DeviceArray while the process default backend is GPU or TPU.
implemented_relation: An unspecified placement request preserves the device of an existing DeviceArray.
validity_obligation: device=None means no placement change for an already committed device array.
root_cause: _copy_device_array_to_device compared the source with a default target even when the caller supplied no target.
physical_effect: The buffer crosses backend through host memory and executes on the default accelerator.
consequence: CPU slicing and summation run on TPU/GPU and can exhaust accelerator memory.
repair: PR 2907 returns the input unchanged when device is None, performs copies only for explicit targets, and adds multi-backend indexing and sum regressions.
observed_decision: _copy_device_array_to_device compared the source with a default target even when the caller supplied no target.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 2907 returns the input unchanged when device is None, performs copies only for explicit targets, and adds multi-backend indexing and sum regressions.
review_note: The issue identifies asarray/device_put, and the patch changes device=None semantics with the reported cross-backend tests.

title: vmap(pmap) different results than map(pmap)
trigger: vmap batches q while an inner pmap maps pts on axis zero and treats q as unmapped.
implemented_relation: Axis movement across nested map transformations depends on whether each pmap operand is mapped by the inner map.
validity_obligation: Nested-map axis adjustment uses each operand's mapped_invars flag when inserting or removing the inner device axis.
root_cause: The old batching rule ignored pmap's mapped_invars and applied one axis transformation to mapped and unmapped operands.
physical_effect: The logical batch, device, and value dimensions are permuted in the pmap result.
consequence: vmap(pmap) returns shape 2x2x3 with transposed values instead of the map(pmap) result of shape 3x2x2.
repair: PR 3439 reads mapped_invars, moves an axis only for a mapped inner operand, adjusts each batch dimension by that flag, and adds the reported vmap-of-pmap comparison.
observed_decision: The old batching rule ignored pmap's mapped_invars and applied one axis transformation to mapped and unmapped operands.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 3439 reads mapped_invars, moves an axis only for a mapped inner operand, adjusts each batch dimension by that flag, and adds the reported vmap-of-pmap comparison.
review_note: The maintainer diagnosis names mapped_invars, and the linked patch uses that field in the failing BatchTrace path and adds the issue reproducer.

title: jnp.asarray does not copy when copy=True
trigger: jnp.asarray does not copy when copy=True
physical_effect: jnp.array(copy=True) retains the input device buffer instead of allocating independent storage, so donation of the original invalidates the supposed copy.
consequence: After a jitted TPU computation donates the original, accessing the copy raises CopyToHostAsync called on invalid buffer.
observed_decision: The array-construction path satisfies an explicit copy request by reusing the existing device buffer because the runtime lacked a device-buffer copy operation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The minimal reproducer combines explicit copy and donation, and a maintainer confirms the runtime lacked buffer copying and proposes a host-bounce implementation until native support exists.
review_note: The report establishes that copy=True reuses the donated buffer and records a host-bounce proposal, but no implemented copy repair or fixed regression is linked.

title: JAX/TF2 on multi-GPU silently corrupted computations
trigger: TensorFlow and JAX alternate GPU work on one Python thread while each shared library contains its own StreamExecutor thread-local CUDA-context cache.
implemented_relation: At every outermost StreamExecutor activation, the actual CUDA current context matches the GpuContext required by the entering library.
validity_obligation: An outermost library boundary reasserts the requested CUDA context; cached equality is used only within nested scopes controlled by the same StreamExecutor instance.
root_cause: ScopedActivateContext trusted its private cached context at depth zero, where arbitrary foreign GPU code could have changed the process-level CUDA state.
physical_effect: JAX submits a kernel or buffer operation under a CUDA context different from the context that owns its device pointers.
consequence: The multi-GPU run executes on the wrong GPU and can report an invalid global read or a corrupted aggregate after TensorFlow GPU activity.
repair: Commit 1e336d3 makes every depth-zero activation call cuCtxSetCurrent for the requested context and refresh the thread-local state; it retains cache-based switching for nested scopes and adds a test that changes the context externally between two activations.
observed_decision: ScopedActivateContext trusted its private cached context at depth zero, where arbitrary foreign GPU code could have changed the process-level CUDA state.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 1e336d3 makes every depth-zero activation call cuCtxSetCurrent for the requested context and refresh the thread-local state; it retains cache-based switching for nested scopes and adds a test that changes the context externally between two activations.
review_note: The issue discussion derives the two-private-cache failure and references commit 1e336d3. The commit states that it fixes JAX #3802 when incorporated, changes the exact outermost activation decision, and tests an external context switch between scopes.

title: `from_dlpack` ignores stride information
trigger: A 2-by-2 view selects the first two columns of a 2-by-3 CuPy array and exports shape and stride metadata through DLPack.
implemented_relation: A DLPack tensor's logical indices map through its strides, or import rejects a stride pattern that XLA's compact layout cannot represent.
validity_obligation: Interop either preserves the producer's logical-to-physical index mapping or fails before exposing a differently indexed array.
root_cause: DLPackManagedTensorToBuffer failed to execute stride-to-layout validation because its zero-dimension search result was tested incorrectly.
physical_effect: The imported XLA buffer indexes consecutive elements [0,1,2,3] rather than the sliced coordinates [0,1,3,4].
consequence: JAX returns [[0,1],[2,3]] instead of [[0,1],[3,4]].
repair: TensorFlow commit 28a2d0a compares absl::c_find(dimensions, 0) with dimensions.end(), allowing stride conversion and rejection of layouts that cannot represent the slice.
observed_decision: DLPackManagedTensorToBuffer failed to execute stride-to-layout validation because its zero-dimension search result was tested incorrectly.
reported_repair_or_workaround: TensorFlow commit 28a2d0a compares absl::c_find(dimensions, 0) with dimensions.end(), allowing stride conversion and rejection of layouts that cannot represent the slice.
review_note: The report isolates the wrong buffer at the XLA importer; the maintainer identifies the invalid stride condition and closes the report after the correcting commit.

title: Nested pmap issue on GPU
trigger: Two nested pmaps request backend='cpu' over four configured CPU devices on a GPU host.
implemented_relation: Replica count and device assignment derive from the backend selected for that pmap.
validity_obligation: Every device-count query in pmap replication uses the same explicit backend as device selection and execution.
root_cause: The replication path dropped the backend parameter when deriving local device count.
physical_effect: Logical pmap axes are bound against the wrong backend's device population.
consequence: The nested pmap reproducer fails on a GPU host although the explicitly selected CPU backend has enough devices.
repair: PR 4272 passes backend to local_device_count and adds the nested backend='cpu' regression.
observed_decision: The replication path dropped the backend parameter when deriving local device count.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 4272 passes backend to local_device_count and adds the nested backend='cpu' regression.
review_note: The failure depends on a GPU host despite explicit CPU pmaps, and the linked patch threads backend into the lone device-count query and adds the reproducer.

title: id_print example from docs broken; crash on GPU
trigger: A callback is vectorized or jitted and executed on a GPU through the outfeed implementation.
physical_effect: The compiled f32 callback request is matched to a u32 token-shaped runtime buffer.
consequence: XLA aborts on its outfeed shape-compatibility check.
observed_decision: The GPU runtime consumes an outfeed buffer associated with a different request shape, which maintainers attribute to bad computation interleaving.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Restricting visibility to one GPU made the later reproducer execute, while maintainers continued to track the multi-GPU problem separately.
review_note: The issue closes after a one-GPU observation and links to the still-unrepaired multi-GPU report, not to a source correction. No exact XLA/JAX repair or fixed regression establishes the repaired interleaving relation.

title: experimental.enable_x64 fails for random.uniform
trigger: The same jitted random function is called under different enable_x64 contexts.
implemented_relation: The x64 mode used to canonicalize arguments matches the mode used to select or compile the cached executable on every call.
validity_obligation: Dynamic thread-local configuration participates consistently in canonicalization, cache identity, and C++ dispatch.
root_cause: The C++ jit treated jax_enable_x64 as effectively session-global instead of reading the calling thread's current context.
physical_effect: Executable parameter layout/dtype and the supplied host scalar disagree.
consequence: random.uniform fails with 'want s64[], got s32[]' after context changes.
repair: PR 5604 makes Python x64 state thread-local and keys caches with it; PR 5851 moves the authoritative context state into the C++ jit bridge and adds alternating-context regressions.
observed_decision: The C++ jit treated jax_enable_x64 as effectively session-global instead of reading the calling thread's current context.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 5604 makes Python x64 state thread-local and keys caches with it; PR 5851 moves the authoritative context state into the C++ jit bridge and adds alternating-context regressions.
review_note: The issue localizes the failure to C++ jit state, and the closing patch explicitly moves that state to C++ and names #5532.

title: `host_callback.call` fails on multi-gpu machine
trigger: A host_callback.call executes in a process exposing two GPUs.
physical_effect: The callback transfer consumes an outfeed buffer with a different shape than the compiled request.
consequence: XLA aborts with a shape-compatibility check failure on a multi-GPU machine.
observed_decision: The XLA GPU outfeed request and runtime outfeed buffer are associated with incompatible shapes or device queues.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Maintainers recommend pure_callback or debug.callback and describe a future CustomCall implementation; host_callback was later removed.
review_note: The issue discussion states that the GPU CustomCall mechanism had landed but was not yet used by host_callback, and the issue later closed without confirmation. The inspected history does not provide a host_callback repair and matching fixed regression for this multi-GPU path.

title: host_callback_test.py is failing on multi-GPU platforms
trigger: The host callback test suite runs while several GPU devices are visible.
physical_effect: Requests for one callback are matched to buffers from another callback or device, producing incompatible shapes and blocked feed operations.
consequence: Tests fail with an outfeed shape mismatch and later hang waiting for feed progress.
observed_decision: The discussion attributes failures to one shared feed queue instead of device-specific queues and marks the report as a duplicate of 5577.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Merged PR 6448 disables the test suite on multi-GPU platforms.
review_note: The merged change suppresses execution of the failing tests and does not repair queue identity or callback routing. The primary report 5577 also lacks a landed host_callback repair, so this duplicate cannot yet map to a supported repaired cause.

title: id_tap on CPU crashes with exceptions
trigger: A CPU host callback raises RuntimeError while using the CustomCall implementation rather than outfeed.
physical_effect: C++ terminates the process instead of returning the Python exception to the invoking thread.
consequence: The CPU program aborts, while outfeed-backed GPU and TPU executions report a callback exception.
observed_decision: The callback exception escapes through pybind11 without a status-returning CustomCall boundary.
reported_repair_or_workaround: A later jaxlib version propagates RuntimeError, and id_tap was eventually removed.
review_note: The issue attributes recovery to unspecified XLA CustomCall changes but does not identify or archive the source delta and regression. Later API removal also does not establish the historical repair relationship.

title: `from_dlpack` on transposed torch arrays gives wrong indexing
duplicate_rationale: Reports 7657 and 17784 share the DLPack stride-derived layout, the loss of usable layout identity at the IFRT/JAX boundary, incorrect coordinate indexing, and the same JAX/XLA repair pair. NumPy versus Torch is a producer difference, not a different invalid decision.
trigger: from_dlpack imports a transposed NumPy or Torch array whose minor-to-major layout differs from the JAX device default.
implemented_relation: The physical layout derived from DLPack strides remains attached to the array or is rejected before a consumer assumes default layout.
validity_obligation: A layout is preserved across the interoperability boundary or incompatibility is reported before execution.
root_cause: from_dlpack admitted a nondefault PjRtBuffer although the then-current IFRT Array interface could not expose that layout to JAX consumers.
physical_effect: Logical indices address default-layout coordinates rather than the producer's stride-derived coordinates.
consequence: Printing may show the transposed array, but indexing returns values from the wrong coordinate.
repair: XLA PR 7357 compares the imported layout with the client default and rejects nondefault layouts; JAX PR 18721 adds the transposed-array regression. Later JAX/IFRT layout support permits compact nondefault layouts, but the documented historical repair is the fail-fast boundary.
observed_decision: from_dlpack admitted a nondefault PjRtBuffer although the then-current IFRT Array interface could not expose that layout to JAX consumers.
reported_repair_or_workaround: XLA PR 7357 compares the imported layout with the client default and rejects nondefault layouts; JAX PR 18721 adds the transposed-array regression. Later JAX/IFRT layout support permits compact nondefault layouts, but the documented historical repair is the fail-fast boundary.
review_note: Reports 7657 and 17784 share the DLPack stride-derived layout, the loss of usable layout identity at the IFRT/JAX boundary, incorrect coordinate indexing, and the same JAX/XLA repair pair. NumPy versus Torch is a producer difference, not a different invalid decision.

title: Long CUDA kernels, long overall run times and `CudnnLegacyConvRunner` related errors with `pjit` on ampere GPUs
trigger: A spatially partitioned convolution executes one compiled XLA ConvolutionThunk across replica streams on multiple Ampere GPUs.
implemented_relation: Each cached cuDNN convolution runner is bound to the GPU stream and StreamExecutor for which it was created.
validity_obligation: Runner-cache reuse occurs only for executions on the same stream; a different stream receives a distinct runner cache.
root_cause: ConvolutionThunk stored one unkeyed MaybeFusedConvRunner instead of associating cached runners with their execution streams.
physical_effect: A replica attempts to execute a cuDNN runner carrying state from another StreamExecutor.
consequence: Replica execution reports 'CudnnLegacyConvRunner cached across multiple StreamExecutors'; remaining replicas wait at the NCCL rendezvous and the process aborts.
repair: Commit eb8025b removes the singleton runner cache, adds a mutex-protected map from Stream pointers to MaybeFusedConvRunner instances, and passes GetOrCreateRunner(params.stream) to each convolution execution.
observed_decision: ConvolutionThunk stored one unkeyed MaybeFusedConvRunner instead of associating cached runners with their execution streams.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit eb8025b removes the singleton runner cache, adds a mutex-protected map from Stream pointers to MaybeFusedConvRunner instances, and passes GetOrCreateRunner(params.stream) to each convolution execution.
review_note: The issue reports the same cross-StreamExecutor error quoted by commit eb8025b. A JAX maintainer identifies that commit as the fix for the report's second problem and later confirms its inclusion in jaxlib 0.1.75.

title: Different outputs on subsequent calls of irfft2 with the same input on GPU with double precision
trigger: jnp.fft.irfft2 is called repeatedly on the same complex128 GPU array.
implemented_relation: An out-of-place FFT may read its input without changing bytes that remain bound to the JAX array after the call.
validity_obligation: Backends with destructive C2R behavior copy every affected input precision before invoking CuFFT.
root_cause: The scratch-copy guard matched complex<float>-to-float but omitted complex<double>-to-double.
physical_effect: The first inverse FFT mutates the complex128 device buffer used by later inverse FFT and real-part reads.
consequence: Successive irfft2 calls with the same JAX input produce different outputs.
repair: TensorFlow/XLA commit d502c624 extends the existing non-aliasing scratch-copy condition to complex<double> and double. JAX PR 10133 records the fixed jaxlib version and tests repeated float32 and float64 IRFFTs.
observed_decision: The scratch-copy guard matched complex<float>-to-float but omitted complex<double>-to-double.
reported_repair_or_workaround: TensorFlow/XLA commit d502c624 extends the existing non-aliasing scratch-copy condition to complex<double> and double. JAX PR 10133 records the fixed jaxlib version and tests repeated float32 and float64 IRFFTs.
review_note: The maintainer identifies the known CuFFT C2R mutation and missing double-precision workaround; the cross-referenced upstream commit changes that exact guard, and the JAX regression repeats the operation on one input.

title: `host_callback.call(..., call_with_device=True)` specifies the wrong device
trigger: Two jitted callback calls execute on different platforms in one process and request their originating device.
physical_effect: The callback receives a device identity that is inconsistent with the computation and result placement.
consequence: Both callback invocations print gpu:0 instead of distinct CPU and GPU devices.
observed_decision: The callback's device reconstruction reports gpu:0 for the CPU-originating invocation even though the returned value remains on CPU.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 30cf057 adds device_index selection for SPMD callbacks and documents limitations of the callback device mechanism; host_callback was later deprecated.
review_note: The inspected commit changes explicit SPMD device-index selection but retains the single-device reconstruction path implicated by this report. The issue closes because host_callback is deprecated, without a linked repair or fixed regression for CPU-versus-GPU call_with_device identity.

title: Unexpected device placement for arrays created within a jax.default_device context
trigger: The same jnp.ones or jnp.zeros primitive and shape is evaluated first on one device and then inside a different default-device context.
implemented_relation: An unspecified array placement is resolved from the default device active for that primitive evaluation.
validity_obligation: Cache equivalence includes every configuration value that changes primitive placement semantics.
root_cause: The in-memory primitive cache omitted jax_default_device from its trace-context key.
physical_effect: A constructor inside the new context reuses an executable or value placement bound to the previous device.
consequence: Arrays appear on the first device used for that shape instead of the device selected by the current context.
repair: Commit 7098088 adds jax_default_device to the trace-context tuple and adds cached, uncached, and reset placement regressions.
observed_decision: The in-memory primitive cache omitted jax_default_device from its trace-context key.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 7098088 adds jax_default_device to the trace-context tuple and adds cached, uncached, and reset placement regressions.
review_note: The report identifies memoization, and the fixing commit states that a cache hit ignored the changed default device and adds the reported context transition to its tests.

title: Memory leak in compiled loops closing over large constants
trigger: Repeatedly created jitted loop bodies close over distinct large DeviceArrays and then go out of user scope.
implemented_relation: A compilation cache entry does not outlive the user-visible function whose closure supplies its constant buffers.
validity_obligation: Cache identity may depend on a function without becoming a new owner that extends the function's captured tensor lifetime.
root_cause: The old control-flow caches used strong-reference memoization for function-keyed jaxpr construction.
physical_effect: Each call leaves a large live device buffer reachable through the cache.
consequence: Resident memory and live executable/buffer counts grow by about one gigabyte per iteration in the reproducer.
repair: PR 11461 replaces strong caches with weakref_lru_cache and passes weak references to loop body functions through cached helpers.
observed_decision: The old control-flow caches used strong-reference memoization for function-keyed jaxpr construction.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 11461 replaces strong caches with weakref_lru_cache and passes weak references to loop body functions through cached helpers.
review_note: The maintainer identifies _initial_style_jaxpr as the retaining cache, and the patch changes its ownership semantics at the named sites.

title: Multi-GPU Workflow Hangs
trigger: Local GPU threads initialize one NCCL clique concurrently and one rank finishes ncclCommInitRank before another rank.
implemented_relation: All local participants in an NCCL clique complete communicator initialization before any participant issues a collective using that clique.
validity_obligation: Collective execution begins only after every local rank has completed ncclCommInitRank for the shared clique.
root_cause: Communicator acquisition lacked a clique-wide post-initialization barrier.
physical_effect: One rank holds the page-table lock while waiting for peer collective progress, and the peer waits for that lock inside cudaMalloc during initialization.
consequence: The reported four-GPU JAX collective intermittently deadlocks.
repair: Upstream commit f9df012 stores communicators in clique state and waits until the number of initialized communicators equals the local participant count before notifying readiness.
observed_decision: Communicator acquisition lacked a clique-wide post-initialization barrier.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Upstream commit f9df012 stores communicators in clique state and waits until the number of initialized communicators equals the local participant count before notifying readiness.
review_note: A maintainer reproduces the deadlock and gives the lock cycle in the report; the upstream commit names issue 11637, implements that barrier, and enters JAX through PR 11691's XLA update.

title: `psum` fails with 1 process per GPU
trigger: Four processes each expose one physical GPU whose local stream ordinal can be a nonzero physical ordinal, such as three.
implemented_relation: Each local GPU ordinal resolves to the correct global device ID regardless of gaps in the process-visible ordinal set.
validity_obligation: The local-to-global identity mapping is keyed by the actual local ordinal rather than inferred from vector position.
root_cause: BuildDistributedDevices discarded the ordinal keys from gpu_device_ids and GetGlobalDeviceId interpreted the remaining values as a dense ordinal-indexed vector.
physical_effect: NCCL collective setup fails before communicator selection for processes assigned nonzero GPU ordinals.
consequence: psum raises a RET_CHECK failure because local_device_ordinal 3 is not less than gpu_global_device_ids size 1.
repair: Commit d8d5a36 stores the mapping as map<int, GlobalDeviceId>, preserves it through GPU run options, and resolves an ordinal with map::find; collective locality derives values from the same map.
observed_decision: BuildDistributedDevices discarded the ordinal keys from gpu_device_ids and GetGlobalDeviceId interpreted the remaining values as a dense ordinal-indexed vector.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit d8d5a36 stores the mapping as map<int, GlobalDeviceId>, preserves it through GPU run options, and resolves an ordinal with map::find; collective locality derives values from the same map.
review_note: The landed XLA commit explicitly fixes JAX issue 12119 and replaces the exact dense-vector lookup named in the reported RET_CHECK with a keyed mapping.

title: pure_callback passes jax.DeviceArray to the callback on CPU when not jitted
trigger: A pure callback receives a JAX array in eager execution while the same callback under jit receives a NumPy array.
implemented_relation: The callback boundary presents the documented NumPy host representation in eager and compiled execution.
validity_obligation: All execution modes cross the same device-to-host callback-lowering boundary before invoking user code.
root_cause: pure_callback defined a separate eager implementation that bypassed its lowering semantics.
physical_effect: The callback's argument representation depends on whether jit surrounds the call.
consequence: Outside jit, the callback observes DeviceArray instead of the documented numpy.ndarray and downstream NumPy code fails.
repair: PR 12203 makes dispatch.apply_primitive and the primitive lowering the eager implementation and adds a non-jit ndarray regression.
observed_decision: pure_callback defined a separate eager implementation that bypassed its lowering semantics.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 12203 makes dispatch.apply_primitive and the primitive lowering the eager implementation and adds a non-jit ndarray regression.
review_note: The report contrasts eager and jitted argument types, and the linked fix removes the separate eager callback path and asserts ndarray input without jit.

title: Pickling a JAX array does not preserve its original device
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises jAX array pickling and restoration of original device placement.
physical_effect: Unpickling reconstructs the array under the current/default placement.
consequence: The restored array resides on a different device.
observed_decision: Serialization preserves logical values but not the array's device binding.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Discussion explores storing device information with the pickle.
review_note: The issue remains open without a landed serialization-format change or fixed regression.

title: jax_debug_nans interaction with buffer donation
trigger: A donated-input compiled computation produces NaN while jax_debug_nans requests a de-optimized rerun.
implemented_relation: A diagnostic rerun reads the original logical arguments, so those buffers remain valid until the rerun decision is complete.
validity_obligation: When a runtime diagnostic may rerun a computation, inputs needed by that rerun are not donated during the first execution.
root_cause: JIT preparation honored donate_argnums even when debug_nans enabled the fallback rerun path.
physical_effect: PJRT marks the input buffer deleted after the first execute.
consequence: NaN diagnosis fails with 'Donation requested for invalid buffer' instead of running the de-optimized function.
repair: PR 13144 clears donated-invars whenever jax_debug_nans is enabled for jit, pmap, and pjit and adds regressions for all three paths.
observed_decision: JIT preparation honored donate_argnums even when debug_nans enabled the fallback rerun path.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 13144 clears donated-invars whenever jax_debug_nans is enabled for jit, pmap, and pjit and adds regressions for all three paths.
review_note: The report describes reuse after donation, and the patch suppresses donation under exactly that diagnostic mode with three reproductions.

title: Memory leak when closing over large constants in compiled jax.lax.cond statement
trigger: A short-lived jitted cond closes over a new device array on each invocation and then all user references are deleted.
implemented_relation: A tracing cache preserves reusable jaxpr structure without extending the lifetime of closed-over tensor constants after their callables die.
validity_obligation: Compilation memoization does not create a strong lifetime edge from a global cache to short-lived branch callables and their tensor constants.
root_cause: The cond tracing helper cached the branch callables strongly instead of caching only weakly keyed jaxpr-padding work.
physical_effect: One otherwise unreachable device buffer remains live after each invocation.
consequence: Resident memory grows by about one GiB per iteration and the live-buffer count rises from one to five while no executable remains live.
repair: PR 22610 removes the strong outer cache and adds a weak-reference LRU cache around _pad_jaxpr_constvars; its regression checks that live buffers return to zero.
observed_decision: The cond tracing helper cached the branch callables strongly instead of caching only weakly keyed jaxpr-padding work.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 22610 removes the strong outer cache and adds a weak-reference LRU cache around _pad_jaxpr_constvars; its regression checks that live buffers return to zero.
review_note: A maintainer confirms that removing the named cache eliminates the leak, and the merged patch replaces that cache and adds the issue-specific live-buffer regression.

title: When lowering with repeated inputs the compiled function fails only after a second call.
trigger: A lowered function receives the same array as x and y, returns only x, and is invoked twice after compilation; y is absent from the executable signature.
implemented_relation: The logical call signature maps each flattened argument position to either one retained executable parameter or a removed unused argument, and every dispatch path applies the same map.
validity_obligation: A cached dispatch preserves the lowering-time retained-argument map and filters logical inputs to exactly the executable's parameter sequence before execution.
root_cause: The old fast-path metadata treated the Python argument list as if every position survived lowering, even when the executable had pruned an unused input.
physical_effect: The second invocation submitted two argument buffers to an executable compiled for one parameter.
consequence: The first call returned normally, while the second failed with `Executable expected 1 arguments but got 2`.
repair: Commit 3b35e981 makes cache-miss helpers retain args_flat, derives kept_var_bitvec from the executable's kept_var_idx, stores that bit vector in _MeshExecutableFastpathData, and requires the compatible C++ pjit interface. Its tests cover both pruned and preserved unused arguments.
observed_decision: The old fast-path metadata treated the Python argument list as if every position survived lowering, even when the executable had pruned an unused input.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 3b35e981 makes cache-miss helpers retain args_flat, derives kept_var_bitvec from the executable's kept_var_idx, stores that bit vector in _MeshExecutableFastpathData, and requires the compatible C++ pjit interface. Its tests cover both pruned and preserved unused arguments.
review_note: JAX 0.4.1 does not contain commit 3b35e981, while 0.4.2 does. The commit adds the missing retained-argument bit vector and a regression that passes the same unused array in five argument positions, invokes the function a second time specifically to enter C++ dispatch, and verifies the pruned executable keeps only the used position. The issue exhibits the same first-call/second-call split and executable arity mismatch; later reproduction confirms the original program succeeds on 0.4.23 and 0.4.24.

title: Precision argument for matmul is not respected on Ampere GPUs like the RTX 3090
trigger: A float32 dot requests HIGHEST precision on a TF32-capable GPU while the XLA runtime executable path is enabled.
implemented_relation: The dot operation's requested operand precision determines the computation type used by the emitted GPU GEMM.
validity_obligation: Every GEMM lowering path propagates the HLO precision request to the library computation-type decision.
root_cause: The runtime custom-call boundary omitted precision_config and substituted kDefaultComputePrecision.
physical_effect: cuBLAS rounds float32 operands to TF32 mantissas for a dot that requested full float32 input precision.
consequence: The reported float32 and tensorfloat32 results are identical and differ from the CPU result by about 2.79e-4.
repair: Commit 3febe1a serializes precision_config onto xla.gpu.gemm, decodes it in GEMM and cuBLASLt custom calls, and passes the maximum requested precision to GetBlasComputationType.
observed_decision: The runtime custom-call boundary omitted precision_config and substituted kDefaultComputePrecision.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 3febe1a serializes precision_config onto xla.gpu.gemm, decodes it in GEMM and cuBLASLt custom calls, and passes the maximum requested precision to GetBlasComputationType.
review_note: The assignee states that the issue is fixed in the next jaxlib; the confirmed fixed build contains the assignee's same-day XLA commit whose patch propagates precision_config through the runtime path named in the workaround.

title: `jax.device_put` not working under `multiprocessing`
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises jax.device_put execution from multiprocessing workers.
physical_effect: The transfer targets runtime state that is unavailable or incompatible in the child.
consequence: device_put fails under multiprocessing.
observed_decision: Forked/process-local runtime state does not provide a valid device/client binding for the transfer.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The report contains no completed implementation proposal.
review_note: No source-localized repair, landed patch, or fixed regression is linked.

title: device_put leaks references on numpy inputs
trigger: A NumPy array is transferred with device_put and the resulting JAX array is deleted before another JAX dispatch.
implemented_relation: The runtime reference that keeps a host input alive for an asynchronous device transfer is released after the transfer-backed device value becomes unreachable.
validity_obligation: Host references retained by XLA are reclaimed when Python performs garbage collection, independent of a later JAX dispatch.
root_cause: The release path depended on incidental XLA garbage collection triggered by subsequent execution.
physical_effect: The NumPy object's reference count stays elevated after the device result is deleted.
consequence: Repeated device_put operations retain host inputs and appear as a reference leak.
repair: PR 14887 registers an XLA collection callback with Python's gc.callbacks and adds a weak-reference regression for device_put input release.
observed_decision: The release path depended on incidental XLA garbage collection triggered by subsequent execution.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 14887 registers an XLA collection callback with Python's gc.callbacks and adds a weak-reference regression for device_put input release.
review_note: The report demonstrates that explicit XLA collection releases the input; the merged repair connects Python collection to that same operation and tests the host weak reference.

title: zeros_like does not preserve sharding information
trigger: A jitted computation creates an array with the shape and dtype of an input that was explicitly sharded across devices.
implemented_relation: A constructor result requested to be sharded like an input carries an explicit same-sharding relation into SPMD propagation.
validity_obligation: When two values are required to share a placement, that equality remains explicit until the SPMD partitioner chooses their common sharding.
root_cause: The constructor preserved shape and dtype but omitted the input-to-result sharding relation needed by the partitioner.
physical_effect: The input spans multiple devices while the constructed result is placed on one default device.
consequence: The reported zeros_like result is single-device sharded and fails the equivalence check against the eight-device input sharding.
repair: Commit 72fbdb2 adds shard_alike, which lowers both values to side-effecting Sharding custom calls with one shard-group identifier and the AS group type; its tests check that jitted constructor-like results inherit the input's multi-device sharding.
observed_decision: The constructor preserved shape and dtype but omitted the input-to-result sharding relation needed by the partitioner.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 72fbdb2 adds shard_alike, which lowers both values to side-effecting Sharding custom calls with one shard-group identifier and the AS group type; its tests check that jitted constructor-like results inherit the input's multi-device sharding.
review_note: A JAX maintainer closes report 16080 as a duplicate of 15600. Report 15600 proposes a shard_like primitive as the fix, and the merged commit declares that it fixes 15600, implements that relation, and tests its placement effect.

title: Sharded FFT with JIT gives incorrect results on GPU since 0.4.9
duplicate_rationale: The report bisects the regression to XLA all-to-all support; the maintainer identifies commit 92d3454 as its repair, and two reporters confirm the sharded FFT works after jaxlib 0.4.19.
trigger: A complex64 array is exchanged by lax.all_to_all across two GPUs using a split dimension.
implemented_relation: Each participant exchanges one disjoint byte chunk representing its share of the logical complex elements.
validity_obligation: The complex-to-NCCL multiplier is applied once to transfer counts, while byte offsets partition the original logical buffer exactly once.
root_cause: RunAllToAll incorporated the complex multiplier into element_count before computing chunk_elements and chunk_bytes.
physical_effect: Participants send and receive bytes from incorrect chunk boundaries, leaving the reconstructed complex array with misplaced or invalid values.
consequence: Applying complementary all_to_all operations fails to reconstruct the input and produces a maximum difference of 66.46803, while the real-valued control is exact.
repair: Commit 92d3454 keeps element_count in logical elements, computes byte offsets from logical chunk_elements, and applies the complex multiplier only to the NCCL send and receive counts.
observed_decision: RunAllToAll incorporated the complex multiplier into element_count before computing chunk_elements and chunk_bytes.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 92d3454 keeps element_count in logical elements, computes byte offsets from logical chunk_elements, and applies the complex multiplier only to the NCCL send and receive counts.
review_note: The report bisects the regression to XLA all-to-all support; the maintainer identifies commit 92d3454 as its repair, and two reporters confirm the sharded FFT works after jaxlib 0.4.19.

title: jax_threefry_partitionable + rematerialization doesn't seem to be working together in distributed training
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises partitionable Threefry random generation combined with rematerialization in distributed training.
physical_effect: Recomputed random work is placed or replicated differently from the forward computation.
consequence: Distributed training fails or consumes excessive memory.
observed_decision: Rematerialization and random-key partitioning do not retain the intended sharding/identity relation across the recomputed region.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The issue discussion explores configuration changes.
review_note: No agreed root decision, landed repair, and matching regression are available.

title: Cannot call custom primitive with ordered effect twice in JVP rule
trigger: A JVP rule binds the same ordered-effect primitive for the primal and tangent values; the same failure also appears when an eager caller invokes the primitive twice with the same abstract values.
implemented_relation: Every primitive invocation supplies the current ordered-effect token alongside its explicit data arguments and returns the successor token for the next invocation.
validity_obligation: Each execution builds its complete explicit and hidden input list from the current effect state, then carries the returned token to the next execution.
root_cause: The dispatch cache treated a wrapper that inserts and advances an ordered-effect token as a reusable stateless callable.
physical_effect: The second execution reached the compiled program with one buffer while its input signature required two.
consequence: Differentiating the custom primitive failed with `Execution supplied 1 buffers but compiled program expected 2 buffers`; adding a dummy explicit token only masked the missing hidden input.
repair: Commit e624610 removes the hand-built lowering and cached C++ apply_primitive wrapper, deletes create_cpp_call_for_apply_primitive, and implements op-by-op primitive calls as a cached jax.jit wrapper around prim.bind.
observed_decision: The dispatch cache treated a wrapper that inserts and advances an ordered-effect token as a reusable stateless callable.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit e624610 removes the hand-built lowering and cached C++ apply_primitive wrapper, deletes create_cpp_call_for_apply_primitive, and implements op-by-op primitive calls as a cached jax.jit wrapper around prim.bind.
review_note: The issue reproducer fails on JAX 0.4.18. A second reporter narrows the failure to reuse of create_cpp_call_for_apply_primitive, observes the missing internally prepended token on the second call, and confirms that forcing unsafe_call avoids it. Commit e624610, merged between 0.4.18 and 0.4.23, deletes that exact wrapper and replaces it with jax.jit. A contributor and a JAX collaborator then run the original reproducer successfully on 0.4.23. The commit does not name issue 18068, so the repair attribution rests on the exact removed mechanism and the release-bounded reproduction evidence.

title: jax.lax.all_to_all gives wrong result on complex arrays.
trigger: A complex64 array is exchanged by lax.all_to_all across two GPUs using a split dimension.
implemented_relation: Each participant exchanges one disjoint byte chunk representing its share of the logical complex elements.
validity_obligation: The complex-to-NCCL multiplier is applied once to transfer counts, while byte offsets partition the original logical buffer exactly once.
root_cause: RunAllToAll incorporated the complex multiplier into element_count before computing chunk_elements and chunk_bytes.
physical_effect: Participants send and receive bytes from incorrect chunk boundaries, leaving the reconstructed complex array with misplaced or invalid values.
consequence: Applying complementary all_to_all operations fails to reconstruct the input and produces a maximum difference of 66.46803, while the real-valued control is exact.
repair: Commit 92d3454 keeps element_count in logical elements, computes byte offsets from logical chunk_elements, and applies the complex multiplier only to the NCCL send and receive counts.
observed_decision: RunAllToAll incorporated the complex multiplier into element_count before computing chunk_elements and chunk_bytes.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 92d3454 keeps element_count in logical elements, computes byte offsets from logical chunk_elements, and applies the complex multiplier only to the NCCL send and receive counts.
review_note: The XLA commit explicitly fixes JAX issue 18122, names the double-applied multiplier, and changes the exact count and offset calculations exercised by the report.

title: Buffer donation fails after loading from disk

review_note: The external PR was closed and no upstream JAX repair or fixed donation regression is linked.

title: Wrong behaviour of pallas.atomic_cas
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises pallas atomic_cas behavior for the reported value and memory update.

title: `broadcast_to` raise Disallowed host-to-device transfer when used inside jax.jit
trigger: A jitted broadcast_to closes over Python scalar 0.1 while host-to-device transfers are disallowed.
implemented_relation: A scalar captured during tracing becomes a constant in the compiled graph rather than a runtime host-to-device transfer.
validity_obligation: Trace-time literal conversion preserves compile-time constant status and binds no runtime transfer operation.
