title: process can exit before jax.debug.prints, needs jax.effects_barrier()
trigger: A program dispatches debug prints inside lax.scan and then reaches process exit without an explicit effects barrier.
physical_effect: Pending print callbacks are abandoned before their output is emitted.
consequence: The scan produces no visible debug output although the equivalent eager loop prints all iterations.
observed_decision: The host process can terminate before asynchronous callback effects complete.
reported_repair_or_workaround: jax.effects_barrier completes pending effects; another user reports that 0.4.26 prints without it.
review_note: The 0.4.23-to-0.4.26 history contains no identified process-exit or pending-callback repair tied to this report, and no regression records automatic exit draining. A single later-version observation does not establish the repair delta.

title: GPU not partitioning RNG with jax_threefry_partitionable=True (vmap/scan layers)
trigger: A large random tensor is generated under jit with a named output sharding and jax_threefry_partitionable enabled.
physical_effect: Each participating device is associated with a 10.5 GiB intermediate for the global random tensor.
consequence: Initialization exhausts GPU memory while a list-comprehension formulation avoids the failure.
observed_decision: The compiled random-generation custom call is reported as producing full-size peak buffers rather than the expected partitioned storage.
reported_repair_or_workaround: A later user reports that the reproducer finishes on JAX 0.4.28 with four T4 GPUs.
review_note: A bounded review of the 0.4.27-to-0.4.28 history did not identify a random-placement repair tied to the report, and the issue remains open without maintainer confirmation or a fixed regression. The version observation alone cannot identify the invalid source decision or repair delta.

title: jnp.cumsum is incorrect when sharding over summing axis on GPUs
trigger: jnp.cumsum scans an axis whose partitions require an internal concatenate operand to be padded.
implemented_relation: Elements introduced only to align an SPMD partition are the additive identity when the partitioner's internal concatenate feeds cumulative aggregation.
validity_obligation: Padding created for SPMD shape alignment carries the operation's neutral value before it enters cross-partition aggregation.
root_cause: HandleConcatenate consumed a resharded internal operand without applying PadWithZero.
physical_effect: Padding contributes to partial sums propagated across GPU partitions.
consequence: jnp.cumsum returns incorrect values when the summation axis is split across two, four, or eight GPUs.
repair: XLA PR 12476 applies PadWithZero to each resharded concatenate operand and updates partitioner tests to require masking of padded elements.
observed_decision: HandleConcatenate consumed a resharded internal operand without applying PadWithZero.
reported_repair_or_workaround: XLA PR 12476 applies PadWithZero to each resharded concatenate operand and updates partitioner tests to require masking of padded elements.
review_note: A JAX maintainer maps the report to XLA PR 12476, whose change zeroes padded concatenate operands; the reporter then verifies the corrected nightly build.

title: Passing `DeviceLocalLayout` to `jax.jit` causes incorrect outputs on GPU
trigger: jax.jit receives an uncommitted row-major array while in_shardings requests a different device-local layout.
implemented_relation: The physical layout of the input buffer passed to an executable matches the layout declared for that executable parameter.
validity_obligation: Argument placement checks both sharding and device-local layout before reusing an existing buffer.
root_cause: The Python and C++ shard-argument fast paths treated matching indices or devices as sufficient and omitted layout equality.
physical_effect: The physical buffer is not transposed to the layout encoded in the executable contract.
consequence: A 2x2 input is interpreted as its transpose and produces [[11,31],[21,41]] instead of [[11,21],[31,41]].
repair: JAX PR 23101 threads layouts through shard handlers and device_put; XLA PR 16187 checks the fast-path IFRT array layout and falls back when it differs. The JAX patch adds the reported layout regression.
observed_decision: The Python and C++ shard-argument fast paths treated matching indices or devices as sufficient and omitted layout equality.
reported_repair_or_workaround: JAX PR 23101 threads layouts through shard handlers and device_put; XLA PR 16187 checks the fast-path IFRT array layout and falls back when it differs. The JAX patch adds the reported layout regression.
review_note: Both linked patches name issue 23100 and add layout equality to the exact argument-reuse paths described by the report.

title: Corner-case sharding regression when replacing concrete mesh with abstract mesh
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises jAX sharding constraints using an AbstractMesh after the value's dependency on a concretely sharded input is removed.
physical_effect: The result loses the requested concrete sharding.
consequence: Abstract and concrete mesh variants return differently sharded arrays.
observed_decision: The abstract-mesh constraint is not rebound to the active concrete mesh when a constant replaces the input-dependent value.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 23635 adds a failing test.
review_note: The linked PR contains only the reproducing test and closed without a repair; no landed correction exists.

title: [Pallas TPU] Wrong value when using `input_output_aliases` with multiple arrays
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises pallas TPU input_output_aliases with more than one array.
physical_effect: A result reads or overwrites storage belonging to another aliased array.
consequence: Hardware execution returns wrong values while interpret mode succeeds.
observed_decision: Multiple logical alias declarations are mapped to an incorrect physical input/output correspondence.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Interpret mode is an observed comparison, not a repair.
review_note: The issue remains open without a source-localized alias repair or fixed hardware regression.

title: INVALID_ARGUMENT when copying array in pinned_host memory with device_put(..., may_alias=False)
trigger: device_put copies a donated pinned-host array with may_alias=False and the source array is then deleted.
implemented_relation: The transfer copy policy determines whether the destination owns independent storage or may reuse/donate the source storage.
validity_obligation: A transfer marked may_alias=False produces destination storage whose validity does not depend on later deletion or donation of the source.
root_cause: The sharding path omitted copy semantics when calling the C++ transfer API, which defaulted the operation to input reuse.
physical_effect: The purported copy remains bound to storage that is donated and deleted through the source path.
consequence: block_until_ready on the destination fails with an INVALID_ARGUMENT for a deleted or donated buffer.
repair: JAX PR 24752 carries ALIAS, COPY, and DONATE through shard handlers; XLA PR 19134 exposes and consumes matching REUSE_INPUT, ALWAYS_COPY, and DONATE_INPUT semantics in the C++ transfer APIs.
observed_decision: The sharding path omitted copy semantics when calling the C++ transfer API, which defaulted the operation to input reuse.
reported_repair_or_workaround: JAX PR 24752 carries ALIAS, COPY, and DONATE through shard handlers; XLA PR 19134 exposes and consumes matching REUSE_INPUT, ALWAYS_COPY, and DONATE_INPUT semantics in the C++ transfer APIs.
review_note: The reproducer requires source donation after a disallowed-alias copy, and the paired merged patches explicitly propagate ALWAYS_COPY across the boundary where that request was lost.

title: jax.full allocates memory on the wrong device
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises jnp.full placement when the requested large array is intended for a specific/default host device.
physical_effect: The large allocation is created on the wrong device.
consequence: The program exhausts or uses unintended device memory.
observed_decision: Internal operations select an accelerator/default placement rather than preserving the caller's desired device context.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Wrapping construction in jax.default_device is a workaround.
review_note: No landed factory-placement repair or fixed regression is linked.

title: Crash with jit of ordered io_callback under shard_map and then no shard_map on CPU
trigger: An ordered io_callback is executed through shard_map and then through a single-device jitted function, forcing its sequencing token between different shardings.
implemented_relation: The token orders a later effect after completion of the earlier callback even when the next executable uses a different sharding.
validity_obligation: A token handoff across shardings preserves effect completion and constructs a representation valid for the destination executable.
root_cause: _token_shard_arg delegated token buffers to _array_shard_arg as if they were ordinary arrays with device layouts.
physical_effect: The array resharding path queries a missing on-device layout on the token buffer.
consequence: The second jitted ordered callback aborts at pjrt_client.h with on_device_shape().has_layout().
repair: PR 25930 waits for each incoming token, creates an empty Boolean value on the requested target layout, and adds the shard-map-to-single-device regression.
observed_decision: _token_shard_arg delegated token buffers to _array_shard_arg as if they were ordinary arrays with device layouts.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 25930 waits for each incoming token, creates an empty Boolean value on the requested target layout, and adds the shard-map-to-single-device regression.
review_note: The failing stack enters _token_shard_arg and then ordinary array resharding, while the linked patch replaces that path with an explicit wait and target placement and adds the reported transition as a test.

title: vmap(jnp.asarray)(numpy_array) does not return a JAX array
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises vmap of jnp.asarray over NumPy inputs.
physical_effect: The mapped output remains a NumPy representation rather than a JAX array.
consequence: The API returns the wrong array kind.
observed_decision: Batching allows a NumPy value to pass through the simplest asarray path without establishing JAX array ownership.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 25835 proposes conversion; other merged arraylike cleanups target different call sites.
review_note: The direct PR was not merged and no landed change is shown to fix this vmap path.

title: JAX getting stuck with asynchronous dispatching (CPU backend)
trigger: A CPU executable invokes a host callback whose body dispatches another JAX CPU computation while outer dispatch is asynchronous.
implemented_relation: The callback must complete before the callback-bearing executable can complete, while the callback body may itself require CPU execution resources.
validity_obligation: A callback-bearing CPU execution leaves a schedulable path for reentrant work required by that callback.
root_cause: PjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute retained asynchronous CPU dispatch even when all_loaded_host_callbacks_ was nonempty.
physical_effect: The intra-op thread pool can be filled by callback invocations whose inner computations wait for the same pool.
consequence: The reported vmap/while-loop computation hangs unless asynchronous CPU dispatch is disabled or the result is forced ready earlier.
repair: XLA PR 21980 selects synchronous execution for executables with loaded host callbacks; JAX PR 26160 adds the reported reentrant callback regression.
observed_decision: PjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute retained asynchronous CPU dispatch even when all_loaded_host_callbacks_ was nonempty.
reported_repair_or_workaround: XLA PR 21980 selects synchronous execution for executables with loaded host callbacks; JAX PR 26160 adds the reported reentrant callback regression.
review_note: The issue discussion identifies reentrant callback dispatch, and the linked XLA change gates the execution mode on callback presence while the JAX test preserves the reported deadlock pattern.

title: zeros_like does not match device when used under JIT
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises zeros_like placement under jit when the reference value has a device binding.
physical_effect: The result is placed according to compilation defaults rather than the reference.
consequence: zeros_like returns a tensor on a different device.
observed_decision: Lowering constructs the zero constant without carrying the reference array's device/placement relation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 26045 proposes a primitive-based full_like implementation.
review_note: PR 26045 was not merged and no alternative landed repair is linked.

title: Control the lifetime of host values of the jax.Array.
trigger: A pinned-host JAX array is converted to NumPy without copying and later participates in repeated donation or reuse.
implemented_relation: A zero-copy NumPy array holds an external reference that keeps the backing device buffer alive for the view's lifetime.
validity_obligation: A zero-copy external reference is retained only for the lifetime of the view that requires it; a persistent cache owns only independently copied host data.
root_cause: The conversion path cached every materialized NumPy value without distinguishing copied from zero-copy results.
physical_effect: The external reference holds the device buffer across donation/reuse boundaries longer than intended.
consequence: Repeated donation and conversion crashes unless _npy_value is manually cleared or replaced.
repair: The XLA binding returns whether host conversion copied, and JAX stores _npy_value only when did_copy is true; pinned-host regression tests require no cache.
observed_decision: The conversion path cached every materialized NumPy value without distinguishing copied from zero-copy results.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The XLA binding returns whether host conversion copied, and JAX stores _npy_value only when did_copy is true; pinned-host regression tests require no cache.
review_note: The paired XLA/JAX API change exposes did_copy and uses it as the cache condition, directly implementing the lifetime distinction from the report.

title: TSAN race in //tests:lax_numpy_einsum_test_cpu
trigger: A free-threaded Python build exports a JAX array through bf_getbuffer while garbage collection traverses the memoryview object.
implemented_relation: The exported Py_buffer metadata binds a Python memoryview to the JAX buffer and its external reference.
validity_obligation: Publication of buffer-view metadata is synchronized with Python runtime traversal and retains the backing buffer reference.
root_cause: The handler assumed the POD Py_buffer could be written safely after releasing the GIL.
physical_effect: The GC traversal and memset of the Py_buffer view race on the same memory.
consequence: ThreadSanitizer reports a data race between mbuf_traverse and PyArray_bf_getbuffer.
repair: PR 22946 limits the GIL-released region to blocking buffer operations, then initializes and publishes the view while the GIL is held.
observed_decision: The handler assumed the POD Py_buffer could be written safely after releasing the GIL.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 22946 limits the GIL-released region to blocking buffer operations, then initializes and publishes the view while the GIL is held.
review_note: The TSAN stacks identify the exact read/write conflict, and the linked patch moves the conflicting writes outside the GIL-released region.

title: Creating a mutable array does not preserve its sharding
trigger: mutable_array receives an array distributed over a two-by-two device mesh.
implemented_relation: A mutable array's defensive storage copy preserves the input array's sharding.
validity_obligation: Creating independent mutable storage copies content without changing its device-to-index mapping.
root_cause: The defensive-copy path did not preserve the initialized array's explicit sharding.
physical_effect: The same logical array becomes bound to one device instead of the supplied mesh.
consequence: Reading the new mutable array reports SingleDeviceSharding instead of the original NamedSharding.
repair: PR 26377 uses JAX's sharding-preserving _array_copy for the defensive copy and exposes the mutable buffer's sharding property.
observed_decision: The defensive-copy path did not preserve the initialized array's explicit sharding.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 26377 uses JAX's sharding-preserving _array_copy for the defensive copy and exposes the mutable buffer's sharding property.
review_note: The report shows sharding loss immediately after mutable-array creation, and the patch replaces that exact copy path and asserts preservation before any ref execution.

title: `ref_get` mutates the sharding of the underlying buffer of a mutable array
trigger: ref_get reads a mutable array whose backing buffer has NamedSharding over four devices.
implemented_relation: Discharging a read-only ref operation carries the mutable input buffer's existing sharding into XLA execution.
validity_obligation: Every discharged mutable input is compiled with the sharding of the buffer whose identity and state it aliases.
root_cause: The old ref-discharge path discarded mutable-input shardings when extending the compiled input list.
physical_effect: A logically read-only operation changes the backing buffer's device mapping.
consequence: After ref_get, the mutable buffer reports SingleDeviceSharding instead of its original NamedSharding.
repair: PR 26377 supplies c.sharding for every discharged mutable input instead of UNSPECIFIED and tests sharding before and after a jitted read.
observed_decision: The old ref-discharge path discarded mutable-input shardings when extending the compiled input list.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 26377 supplies c.sharding for every discharged mutable input instead of UNSPECIFIED and tests sharding before and after a jitted read.
review_note: The report isolates sharding change to ref_get, and the patch replaces UNSPECIFIED precisely for discharged mutable inputs and checks the post-read buffer sharding.

title: jax.debug.print Displays Misleading Output for XLA 4-bit Tensors
trigger: A jitted debug.print transfers a packed float4_e2m1fn array through the callback path.
physical_effect: The callback's host values no longer correspond to the logical four-bit tensor elements.
consequence: Jitted debug.print displays values inconsistent with non-jitted printing.
observed_decision: The callback constructs a NumPy array whose element representation has no matching sub-byte dtype, so packed bytes are interpreted through an incompatible host layout.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 27013 proposes converting float4 values to float32 before invoking debug_callback, and the reporter confirms the proposal fixes the example.
review_note: PR 27013 was closed without merge. Reporter confirmation of an unmerged proposal does not establish a landed JAX repair or a durable fixed regression in the studied source history.

title: Segmentation fault when calling exported choleksy on CPU
trigger: A process deserializes and calls an exported Cholesky computation without first tracing another LAPACK operation.
implemented_relation: Every backend referenced by an exported computation is initialized before the deserialized callable dispatches its FFI kernels.
validity_obligation: Deserialized execution initializes platform-specific runtime handlers independently of prior tracing in the process.
root_cause: Export deserialization relied on incidental backend initialization performed by normal lowering.
physical_effect: The CPU executable calls a null LAPACK kernel pointer.
consequence: Calling the rehydrated Cholesky function in a fresh process segfaults on CPU.
repair: PR 33522 adds _ensure_backends_initialized, initializes jaxlib.cpu._lapack for CPU platforms, and invokes it before calling a deserialized export.
observed_decision: Export deserialization relied on incidental backend initialization performed by normal lowering.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 33522 adds _ensure_backends_initialized, initializes jaxlib.cpu._lapack for CPU platforms, and invokes it before calling a deserialized export.
review_note: Tracing first makes the crash disappear, and the linked fix identifies null CPU LAPACK handlers and initializes them in the deserialized-export path.

title: No error message but failing zero-copy?
trigger: jnp.from_dlpack imports a PETSc vector whose address does not satisfy JAX's zero-copy alignment requirement and explicitly requests copy=False.
implemented_relation: copy=False either aliases the producer storage or reports that zero-copy import is impossible; it does not return independent storage.
validity_obligation: The copy policy reaches the component that chooses between reusing producer storage, allocating a copy, and rejecting the import.
root_cause: dlpack_managed_tensor_to_buffer did not receive copy and silently used its CPU fallback when zero-copy buffer creation failed.
physical_effect: JAX mutations update the copied buffer rather than the PETSc-owned allocation.
consequence: Pointer or value checks show that the PETSc view does not observe the JAX update despite copy=False and no corresponding error.
repair: PR 29963 passes copy into the native importer: False disables fallback and raises when copying is required, True performs a copy, and None retains the permitted fallback policy.
observed_decision: dlpack_managed_tensor_to_buffer did not receive copy and silently used its CPU fallback when zero-copy buffer creation failed.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 29963 passes copy into the native importer: False disables fallback and raises when copying is required, True performs a copy, and None retains the permitted fallback policy.
review_note: Maintainers map the report to PR 29963 and later explain its alignment-specific behavior; the merged patch threads copy through the exact native fallback and adds aligned and misaligned tests.

title: Bug in `out_shardings`?
trigger: Eager with_sharding_constraint receives an uncommitted JAX array and an equivalent SingleDeviceSharding.
implemented_relation: The eager constraint promises an output array committed to the requested sharding.
validity_obligation: Applying an eager output-sharding constraint materializes the output semantics, including commitment, even when placement is already equivalent.
root_cause: The fast path equated sharding equivalence with full output-semantic equivalence and returned x unchanged.
physical_effect: No identity executable or device transfer creates a newly committed array object.
consequence: with_sharding_constraint returns committed=False while device_put with the same sharding returns committed=True.
repair: PR 31203 removes both equivalent-sharding forwarding branches and always runs the identity jit for eager constraints.
observed_decision: The fast path equated sharding equivalence with full output-semantic equivalence and returned x unchanged.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 31203 removes both equivalent-sharding forwarding branches and always runs the identity jit for eager constraints.
review_note: The maintainer points to the forwarding shortcut, and the patch removes only that shortcut and asserts commitment in the regression.

title: vjp3 + array refs produce incorrect gradient
trigger: A reverse backward scan accumulates gradients through mutable array references.
implemented_relation: Each reverse-scan iteration reads and updates the mutable-ref slot for the logical element processed in that iteration.
validity_obligation: State discharge maps the physical counter to length - counter - 1 whenever scan reverse is true.
root_cause: The old discharge rule ignored the reverse flag when indexing mutable-ref inputs and updates.
physical_effect: The accumulated gradient tensor is reversed along the scanned layer dimension.
consequence: vjp3 with refs follows a different loss curve and converges much more slowly than the non-ref gradient baseline.
repair: PR 32438 separates the increasing counter i_ from logical index i, computes i = length - i_ - 1 for reverse scans, and adds a reverse-vjp3 mutable-ref regression.
observed_decision: The old discharge rule ignored the reverse flag when indexing mutable-ref inputs and updates.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 32438 separates the increasing counter i_ from logical index i, computes i = length - i_ - 1 for reverse scans, and adds a reverse-vjp3 mutable-ref regression.
review_note: The reporter identifies an exactly reversed gradient, and the merged patch applies reverse indexing at the mutable-array discharge rule and tests the vjp3 path.

title: Case where `device_put` creates a malformed McJAX array
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises multi-controller JAX device_put construction of a global array.
physical_effect: Array metadata and addressable buffers disagree about shard ownership.
consequence: The resulting array is malformed.

reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 35808 is proposed in the discussion.
review_note: No merged repair and fixed multiprocess regression are present in the evidence.

title: bool to int32 conversion broken / inconsistent
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises stableHLO boolean-to-integer conversion for noncanonical boolean byte representations.
physical_effect: A true byte such as 0xff becomes integer 255 rather than 1.
consequence: JAX conversion returns values inconsistent with StableHLO semantics.
observed_decision: XLA converts the underlying byte value instead of logical false/true semantics.

title: jax parallelism and tensorflow
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises jAX multi-GPU execution in a process that also imports TensorFlow.
physical_effect: JAX collective execution fails after TensorFlow import.
consequence: Parallel execution does not complete correctly.

title: Inconsistent value dependent device for boolean masked array
trigger: Boolean masking produces an empty output shape from an array committed to a nondefault CPU device.
implemented_relation: The gather indexer derives the output slice sharding from the indexed array, including its concrete single-device placement.
validity_obligation: An empty-result fast path preserves the concrete placement implied by the indexed source when no data-dependent transfer occurs.
root_cause: _gather constructed the empty result without a usable concrete slice sharding.

title: [inductor][while_loop] cond_fn-only mutation of a pre-mutated captured tensor is not replayed

title: [Inductor] Direct generalized_scatter copy-back changes returned output aliasing

title: [ROCm][Inductor] `as_strided` on a graph-input view reads back zeros when the rebased offset is negative

title: [inductor] `x[1:] = x[:-1].clone()` compiles to a copy over overlapping memory: silent wrong results on CUDA and CPU
trigger: A row shift assigns x[:-1].clone() into x[1:], after a prior pass has removed the clone while the graph still has functional scatter semantics.

validity_obligation: Scatter reinplacing is allowed only when its source storage is independent of the storage that the mutating decomposition overwrites.
root_cause: The in-place safety test considered future consumers of the destination but omitted the storage identity of another operand used by the mutation itself.

repair: Commit 0f9fcef obtains the storage identities of the generalized-scatter input and source and declines reinplacing when they match. The functional decomposition then retains its cloned base. It adds the reported row-shift regression on CPU.
observed_decision: The in-place safety test considered future consumers of the destination but omitted the storage identity of another operand used by the mutation itself.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 0f9fcef obtains the storage identities of the generalized-scatter input and source and declines reinplacing when they match. The functional decomposition then retains its cloned base. It adds the reported row-shift regression on CPU.

title: [inductor] Autograd's "modified by an inplace operation" check is lost when a view of a graph input is saved for backward: `x @ w`, `bmm`, `einsum`, 3-D `F.linear` silently return wrong gradients after `x` is modified in place

physical_effect: Inductor reconstructs a view saved for backward as a new TensorImpl on the input's storage but with an independent version counter.
consequence: In-place modification between forward and backward no longer raises and backward silently computes gradients from mutated data belonging to no executed forward pass.
observed_decision: Graph-escaping saved views use _reinterpret_tensor rather than alias regeneration from the graph input, severing the version-counter relation that represents mutation history.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Backend/operator matrix, saved-tensor pointer and version probes, and AOT graph inspection isolate the missing shared counter; the proposed fix reuses input-alias regeneration for saved views.
review_note: The report proposes regenerating saved aliases from the graph input, but no landed repair or fixed regression demonstrates restored version-counter sharing.

title: [inductor] `x + 0` / `x * 1` / `x / 1.0` as a graph output returns the input tensor itself (`out is x`), so an in-place update of the result silently corrupts the input
trigger: [inductor] `x + 0` / `x * 1` / `x / 1.0` as a graph output returns the input tensor itself (`out is x`), so an in-place update of the result silently corrupts the input
physical_effect: Joint-graph no-op elimination replaces a fresh arithmetic result at the graph boundary with its input tensor, introducing input/output aliasing absent from eager semantics.
consequence: For neutral values such as x+0 or x/1, mutating the returned tensor silently mutates the caller's input; non-neutral values remain independent.
observed_decision: replace_no_op calls replace_all_uses_with on output-producing identity operations without the storage-alias guard already used by the post-grad no-op pass.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Backend, value, device, dtype, and requires-grad controls localize the change to joint_graph.remove_no_ops; applying the existing output-alias guard restores eager behavior.
review_note: A local guard restores eager alias behavior, but no landed patch or fixed-version regression establishes the repository repair.

title: [inductor] y = x.clone(); op(y, x) becomes op(x, x) for custom ops and user-defined Triton kernels that mutate x: silent wrong results
trigger: A graph clones x and passes the clone as a read argument to an operation that mutates x.
physical_effect: The compiled operation receives x for both its source and destination, so reads race or follow earlier writes.
consequence: The custom-op reproducer returns a partially mirrored vector and the Triton reproducer has many mismatched elements.
observed_decision: Clone removal and reinplacement consider later uses but omit another argument of the same mutating node that reads the storage.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 198260 proposes retaining a clone when another argument reads storage that the node mutates.
review_note: The existing repair for report 197829 covers overlapping scatter copies, not custom-op or user-kernel argument aliasing. Direct PR 198260 was not merged, so no landed change and fixed regression close this report's repair chain.

title: [inductor] torch._foreach_add_([x], [x.flip(0)]) reads x while writing it: silent wrong results (CUDA and CPU)
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises torchInductor in-place foreach lowering when a result reads a transformed view of the same destination.
physical_effect: The fused kernel reads destination elements while other iterations overwrite them.
consequence: CPU and CUDA executions silently return wrong values.
observed_decision: The lowering assigns MutationLayout directly to a pointwise result whose reads are not position-identical to its writes.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PRs 198242 and 198549 propose preserving a copy or preventing realized-buffer storage swinging.
review_note: Both direct repair proposals were unmerged at the study boundary; no landed patch and fixed regression establish the repair.

title: AOTInductor drops the storage offset of a mutable view argument under dynamic shapes (missing lowering for aten.sym_storage_offset)
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises dynamic-shape AOTInductor handling of mutable view arguments whose storage offset is symbolic.
physical_effect: Writes intended for a disjoint view land at the beginning of the base buffer.
consequence: Two mutable slices overwrite the wrong physical region and return wrong sums.

title: [inductor] Scatter result reinplaced into a graph input that a later, unrelated mutation overwrites: y = slice_scatter(x, src); x.zero_(); return y returns zeros
trigger: A functional result may be reinplaced into a graph input, an unrelated copy or mutation later overwrites that input, and the result is observed afterward.
implemented_relation: Reinplacement makes the functional result and graph input share storage.
validity_obligation: If a later write replaces the input with a value unrelated to the reinplaced result, neither the result nor any value that would share its buffer remains observable afterward.
root_cause: The placeholder branch checked for a copy-back and intervening input-view uses but not the copy source or post-copy liveness of the result alias closure.
physical_effect: The later input write replaces bytes that still represent the returned functional result.
consequence: The returned scatter result contains zeros or fill values instead of the eager result.
repair: The pass computes values that would alias the result, checks whether copy_ writes one of them, and rejects reinplacement when an unrelated copy precedes any later use of that alias set.
observed_decision: The placeholder branch checked for a copy-back and intervening input-view uses but not the copy source or post-copy liveness of the result alias closure.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The pass computes values that would alias the result, checks whether copy_ writes one of them, and rejects reinplacement when an unrelated copy precedes any later use of that alias set.

title: [inductor] Consumer of a dtype view of an input is computed after a later in-place mutation of that input (y = x.view(int32) * 2; y.sub_(-4); x[:, 2:5] = 2; return y.view(int64))
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises torchInductor scheduling of consumers of dtype views across a later mutation of the aliased input.
physical_effect: The consumer is computed after the input mutation and observes new values.

title: [inductor] `dst[:] = src[:]; src.add_(1)` copies the *updated* `src` into `dst` (remove_noop_ops replaces a copy of an input by the input itself, which is mutated before the copy's user runs)
trigger: [inductor] `dst[:] = src[:]; src.add_(1)` copies the *updated* `src` into `dst` (remove_noop_ops replaces a copy of an input by the input itself, which is mutated before the copy's user runs)
physical_effect: Post-grad no-op elimination replaces a snapshot copy from a graph input with the input itself even though that input is mutated before the snapshot's later consumer executes.
consequence: The destination copy reads source values after add_, mul_, or index_fill_ rather than the pre-mutation values specified by eager order.
observed_decision: remove_noop_ops checks introduced input/output aliasing but not whether a non-view copy's substituted source has an earlier mutation than one of the removed node's users.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Correct SSA graph and generated wrapper show the copy eliminated and write-backs reversed; source-view and input-order controls explain when it fails, and the proposed mutation-order guard preserves required copies.

title: [inductor] x.index_put_(...) followed by x.add_(x.flip(0)): the copy back into x is fused with a read of x at other positions (silent wrong results, CUDA and CPU)
trigger: x.index_put_(...) is followed by x.add_(x.flip(0)), so the second mutation reads the same storage at reversed positions.
implemented_relation: Every versioned name produced by an in-place mutation continues to identify the same backing storage for dependency checks against later mutations.
validity_obligation: Before fusing a reader with a later mutation, read identities are resolved through the mutation chain and differing read/write indices remain ordered across kernels.
root_cause: The dependency check resolved the later mutation to its real buffer but compared each read's unresolved versioned name.
physical_effect: One kernel reads x at reversed positions while writing x, allowing reads to observe elements already changed by other iterations.
consequence: The reported program returns widespread silent value mismatches on CPU and CUDA, including about one million differing elements at shape 1024 by 2048.
repair: Commit 8513bdd resolves every candidate read through mutation_real_name before comparing it with the mutated buffer. It adds the report's index_put_-then-flip regression.
observed_decision: The dependency check resolved the later mutation to its real buffer but compared each read's unresolved versioned name.

title: [inductor] x.copy_(x.transpose(-1, -2) * 1.0) on CUDA: a weak dep pruned before loop reordering lets the copy fuse with a transposed read (silent wrong results, regression)

physical_effect: The fused kernel reads transposed elements while writing the same storage.
consequence: Large CUDA inputs produce nondeterministic wrong elements.
observed_decision: A weak mutation dependency is pruned before loop reordering, and the reordered producer no longer satisfies the positional-read condition used to prune it.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 198328 proposes preventing loop reordering across the read/mutate pair.

title: Since 2.13, inductor's 4x random path corrupts CUDA dropout masks
trigger: Dropout consumes a materialized transpose and is compiled into a one-dimensional forward kernel, while checkpoint recomputation can use a differently tiled kernel.
implemented_relation: A given logical RNG element maps to the same independent random word regardless of physical offset order or kernel tiling.
validity_obligation: Vectorized random generation is selected only when offset grouping preserves one-to-one logical RNG identity and every recomputation uses the same seed-offset-to-word mapping.
root_cause: The selection rule used generated-kernel dimensionality as a proxy for offset contiguity and did not preserve the RNG mapping across alternative legal tilings.
physical_effect: Groups of channels receive duplicate random words, while checkpoint forward and recompute obtain independent masks from identical functional RNG state.
consequence: Compiled inference shows 100% duplication within four-channel groups, and checkpoint forward/backward mask agreement falls to about 50% at p=0.5, producing silent wrong gradients.
repair: Commit 983d11f adds an explicit use_rand4x configuration gate that is disabled by default and updates random-codegen tests to exercise the safe tl.rand default while retaining opt-in rand4x coverage.
observed_decision: The selection rule used generated-kernel dimensionality as a proxy for offset contiguity and did not preserve the RNG mapping across alternative legal tilings.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit 983d11f adds an explicit use_rand4x configuration gate that is disabled by default and updates random-codegen tests to exercise the safe tl.rand default while retaining opt-in rand4x coverage.
review_note: The report traces both failures to the rand4x selection path and shows that disabling only that path restores independent masks and checkpoint agreement. Landed commit 983d11f directly references 198333 and disables rand4x by default at the identified selection guard.

title: flex_attention returns incorrect output under Inductor when seq_len < block size
trigger: A sequence shorter than 128 uses the decoding kernel, and a pointwise scale produces q from a [B,S,H,D] view before FlexAttention lowering.
implemented_relation: Every stride baked into the decoding GQA view describes the final physical layout chosen for the realized query buffer.
validity_obligation: Lowering freezes a flexible producer's physical layout before exporting its strides into any fixed view or kernel interface.
root_cause: Stride metadata was consumed as a stable physical contract although its owning buffer could still change layout during scheduling.
physical_effect: The decode kernel maps logical q head and sequence coordinates to wrong physical offsets in the realized pointwise buffer.
consequence: For sequence lengths 32 and 64 with a pointwise q/k producer, compiled FlexAttention differs from the matching SDPA result by about 0.90 to 0.96; direct q/k inputs and lengths at least 128 are correct.
repair: Commit 17b697f freezes the realized query through as_storage_and_layout before reading its strides and constructing the GQA view. It adds a short-query pointwise-producer regression for MHA and GQA configurations.
observed_decision: Stride metadata was consumed as a stable physical contract although its owning buffer could still change layout during scheduling.

title: Misaligned address in triton kernel
trigger: A kernel derives x1 with integer division and forms a store address x0 + 1185*x1 into a view whose row stride is not 16-byte aligned.
implemented_relation: The divisibility attached to a computed index is a sound lower bound on the alignment of every address represented by that index.
validity_obligation: Vector width is selected only from divisibility facts preserved by the complete arithmetic expression.
root_cause: Division analysis inferred nontrivial divisibility for constant divisors other than one.
physical_effect: Code generation emits a vector store at an address not aligned for that vector width.
consequence: The generated CUDA kernel fails with a misaligned-address error.
repair: PR 1341 makes division conservatively return divisibility one except for zero and division by one, and updates alignment-analysis tests.
observed_decision: Division analysis inferred nontrivial divisibility for constant divisors other than one.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 1341 makes division conservatively return divisibility one except for zero and division by one, and updates alignment-analysis tests.

title: Incorrect behavior from mutation
trigger: RBLOCK spans multiple warps while a loaded value is broadcast across the reduction dimension and the source address is overwritten.
physical_effect: Some threads can load after another thread stores the incremented value.
consequence: The device assertion intermittently observes a nonzero pre-mutation value.
observed_decision: The generated program assumes a cross-warp read-before-write order without installing a fence.
reported_repair_or_workaround: tl.debug_barrier is suggested manually; Triton-CPU PR 89 only lowers that operation to a CPU no-op.

title: `tl.device_assert` can observe incorrect results from `tl.associative_scan`
trigger: A 32-element scan runs with four warps, or a smaller scan dimension repeats data across lanes.
implemented_relation: Each unique logical element contributes once to the prefix scan even when the layout replicates that element across lanes or warps.
validity_obligation: Warp and inter-warp scan steps use unique-data lane and warp counts; replicated participants only receive the resulting value.
root_cause: ScanLoweringHelper used total threads per warp and initially incompletely handled repeated warps, so layout replication entered the reduction domain.
physical_effect: Internal lanes observe prefixes 33 through 128 for a 32-element scan, or repeated 1-through-32 sequences for a 16-element scan.
consequence: tl.device_assert observes invalid prefixes, and consumers that use the scan for indices can derive out-of-range coordinates even when the final stored tensor is broadcast-correct.
repair: PR 2330 separates warps with unique data from repetitive warps. PR 2345 adds the unique-data thread count, uses it throughout warp and partial-reduce lowering, and extends the regression to scan sizes 1 and 16.
observed_decision: ScanLoweringHelper used total threads per warp and initially incompletely handled repeated warps, so layout replication entered the reduction domain.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 2330 separates warps with unique data from repetitive warps. PR 2345 adds the unique-data thread count, uses it throughout warp and partial-reduce lowering, and extends the regression to scan sizes 1 and 16.
review_note: The issue reports the two replication failures; the two linked merged patches repair repeated warps and then repeated threads, and the final regression covers both reported small dimensions.

title: Reduction Op on MMA Layout produces incorrect results
trigger: A Hopper MMA v3 layout distributes more than four warps across two dimensions and then reduces a tensor encoded in that layout.
implemented_relation: The layout maps a linear execution ID to separate warp and lane coordinates; Hopper fixes warp order to [0,1] while thread order remains [1,0].
validity_obligation: Every lowering that maps warp IDs to tensor coordinates uses the architecture-defined warp order independently of lane order.
root_cause: The layout exposed one getOrder result for both warp and thread coordinate calculations.
physical_effect: Reduction participants and offsets are associated with incorrect multidimensional warp coordinates.
consequence: The eight-warp MMA-layout reduction deterministically returns incorrect values, including values outside the expected softmax range.
repair: PR 3970 adds getWarpOrder, forces Hopper MMA warp order [0,1], retains the existing thread order, updates consumers, and enables an eight-warp reduction regression.
observed_decision: The layout exposed one getOrder result for both warp and thread coordinate calculations.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 3970 adds getWarpOrder, forces Hopper MMA warp order [0,1], retains the existing thread order, updates consumers, and enables an eight-warp reduction regression.
review_note: The failing case requires a two-dimensional eight-warp MMA v3 layout, and the merged patch separates the exact two orders previously conflated and exercises that configuration in the reduction test.

title: Triton interpreter cannot handle parameters that alias
trigger: Triton interpreter cannot handle parameters that alias
physical_effect: The Triton interpreter creates independent host copies for aliased kernel parameters and copies each parameter back separately, losing their shared physical-storage relation.
consequence: A store through the first alias is overwritten during copy-back by the untouched second alias, so a kernel that writes one returns the original zero.
observed_decision: Argument staging is performed per parameter without grouping identical or overlapping storage ranges into one shared host backing allocation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The one-element identical-argument reproducer isolates staging; maintainers acknowledge the bug and outline parent-storage grouping with best-effort overlap support.
review_note: The maintainers outline storage-range grouping, but no implemented interpreter repair or fixed test is available.

title: Triton incorrectly interprets uint8 indices as int8 in pointer arithmetic operations
trigger: A uint8 tensor containing offsets 128 through 255 is added to a source pointer before tl.load.
implemented_relation: An unsigned logical index denotes the same nonnegative element offset when widened for pointer arithmetic.
validity_obligation: Pointer lowering widens an unsigned offset with zero extension before any operation that otherwise assigns signed meaning to the signless bits.
root_cause: semantic.add discarded the source unsignedness at the tt.addptr boundary.
physical_effect: Loads address elements before the source pointer rather than elements 128 through 255 after it.
consequence: The first 128 results are correct, while later loads return the sentinel values stored before the source slice.
repair: Commit b5af392 zero-extends unsigned offsets narrower than 64 bits to i64 before creating tt.addptr and adds a frontend IR assertion for the extension.
observed_decision: semantic.add discarded the source unsignedness at the tt.addptr boundary.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Commit b5af392 zero-extends unsigned offsets narrower than 64 bits to i64 before creating tt.addptr and adds a frontend IR assertion for the extension.
review_note: The report's uint8 boundary behavior matches the pre-existing addptr bug exactly; the maintainer states top of tree is fixed, and the landed patch zero-extends the same unsigned narrow offsets before addptr.

title: Potential bug of memory descriptor of WGMMA.cpp
trigger: A K=64 shared-memory operand is split into multiple K=16 WGMMA subtiles under a swizzled layout.
implemented_relation: A logical subview coordinate maps to the physical address defined by the descriptor's swizzled shared-memory layout.
validity_obligation: Subview address calculation incorporates layout order, swizzle stride, tile size, element width, and existing descriptor offsets.
root_cause: The old generic memdesc_subview rule treated NVMMASharedEncodingAttr like an unswizzled strided encoding.
physical_effect: WGMMA loads bytes from the wrong shared-memory tile for later repetitions.
consequence: K=64 matrix multiplication returns incorrect results after subtiling while K=32 may pass.
repair: PR 6241 adds NVMMASharedEncodingAttr-specific offset arithmetic based on swizzle stride, tile size, layout order, descriptor offsets, and element bit width, plus a lowering regression.
observed_decision: The old generic memdesc_subview rule treated NVMMASharedEncodingAttr like an unswizzled strided encoding.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 6241 adds NVMMASharedEncodingAttr-specific offset arithmetic based on swizzle stride, tile size, layout order, descriptor offsets, and element bit width, plus a lowering regression.
review_note: Maintainers identify shared-memory subview addressing, and the patch replaces the generic stride formula for the reported encoding.

title: Loading from TMA descriptor hangs
trigger: Autotuning selects BLOCK_SIZE=512 for a descriptor load shaped [512,16] on GH200.
implemented_relation: The set of TMA messages covers the complete logical block, and barrier completion expects exactly the bytes those messages request.
validity_obligation: Each hardware TMA block dimension stays within 256 elements, with larger logical blocks partitioned into enough messages to cover every element and byte.
root_cause: Descriptor lowering mapped a logical dimension larger than 256 directly to one TMA block dimension.
physical_effect: The issued transfer accounts for fewer bytes than the barrier's expected transaction count.
consequence: The kernel spins indefinitely in the TMA barrier wait and stalls the autotuner.
repair: PR 6776 derives a hardware-sized TMA block shape, creates a message-to-offset layout, and emits multiple messages for larger logical dimensions.
observed_decision: Descriptor lowering mapped a logical dimension larger than 256 directly to one TMA block dimension.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 6776 derives a hardware-sized TMA block shape, creates a message-to-offset layout, and emits multiple messages for larger logical dimensions.
review_note: A maintainer identifies silent hardware truncation and the full-byte barrier wait; the merged repair is explicitly titled and described as splitting dimensions above 256.

title: Using triton.autotune with the kernel updated in place will result in incorrect output
trigger: The autotuner executes multiple configurations of an in-place scaling kernel against the same logits buffer.
physical_effect: Candidate configurations scale already modified logits instead of one common initial value.
consequence: Autotuning produces an incorrect final output for the in-place buffer.
observed_decision: Repeated benchmark executions observe state produced by prior candidate executions unless the caller supplies a suitable restore policy.
reported_repair_or_workaround: The report mentions reset_to_zero and restore_value controls but does not establish their intended combination for this mutation.
review_note: The issue was closed as not planned without maintainer analysis, contract clarification, implementation change, or fixed regression. The available record cannot distinguish a tool defect from unsupported stateful-autotune use or identify a repair.

title: Scalar vs. Tensor atomic, Sychornization & Broadcasting Behavior
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises triton lowering of scalar and tensor atomic acquire loops with inactive lanes.
physical_effect: Inactive lanes keep the acquire loop active after participating lanes succeed.
consequence: The tensor lock implementation deadlocks.
observed_decision: Inactive lanes retain a default result that fails the loop-exit comparison, while scalar lowering uses shared-memory broadcast and barriers.
reported_repair_or_workaround: A commenter proposes predicate-select fixes for AtomicCAS and AtomicRMW.
review_note: No linked pull request, landed commit, or fixed regression supports the proposed change; the issue remains open.

title: CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS on Broadcast -> Dot when num_stages > 2
trigger: A broadcast operand with a 32- or 64-byte per-stage tile is loaded through TMA in a kernel using more than one pipeline stage.
implemented_relation: Each logical pipeline stage maps to a shared-memory slice whose address must satisfy TMA's 128-byte alignment requirement.
validity_obligation: Every stage address passed to a TMA load is 128-byte aligned, not only the base allocation.
root_cause: XLA's CanUseTma selected TMA without combining broadcast consumption, pipeline depth, and per-stage tile-byte alignment.
physical_effect: A later descriptor load accesses a misaligned shared-memory address.
consequence: The reported kernel raises CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS for three or four stages; related XLA search cases crash Triton's pipeliner.
repair: XLA PR 47198 disables TMA when num_stages > 1, the operand feeds a broadcast, and tile_byte_size is not divisible by 128; tests retain TMA for aligned and unpipelined cases.
observed_decision: XLA's CanUseTma selected TMA without combining broadcast consumption, pipeline depth, and per-stage tile-byte alignment.
reported_repair_or_workaround: XLA PR 47198 disables TMA when num_stages > 1, the operand feeds a broadcast, and tile_byte_size is not divisible by 128; tests retain TMA for aligned and unpipelined cases.
review_note: Triton maintainers identify the 128-byte stage-offset failure, and the merged XLA patch encodes and tests that exact predicate while labeling itself temporary.

title: `tl.atomic_add` is not correct across threads
trigger: A tensor tl.atomic_add has one active element, and its returned index is broadcast and consumed by stores from a wider thread set.
implemented_relation: Every consumer of a broadcasted tensor atomic result must receive the value produced by a participating atomic lane.
validity_obligation: When a tensor atomic result is consumed under a wider layout, lowering supplies each consumer with the corresponding participating result.
root_cause: Atomic lowering returned per-thread values without materializing the cross-thread distribution required by the result layout.
physical_effect: Store addresses computed by nonparticipating threads use zero or undefined atomic-return values.
consequence: Only one element is written at the expected output row while the remaining stores target the wrong row.
repair: PR 7460 allocates scratch storage when a tensor atomic result requires broadcasting, stores participating results, synchronizes, reloads them for consumers, and adds used-result and unused-result tests.
observed_decision: Atomic lowering returned per-thread values without materializing the cross-thread distribution required by the result layout.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 7460 allocates scratch storage when a tensor atomic result requires broadcasting, stores participating results, synchronizes, reloads them for consumers, and adds used-result and unused-result tests.
review_note: The maintainer identifies undefined values in nonparticipating threads, and the merged patch implements and tests the missing distribution only when the returned value is used.

title: Dot crashes or produce incorrect results with float16 and N==8 on H100
trigger: A matmul uses BLOCK_N=8, selects WGMMA, and places its right-hand operand in an unswizzled shared-memory layout.
implemented_relation: The WGMMA descriptor and per-instruction offset identify the exact shared-memory submatrix supplying each logical right-hand operand tile.
validity_obligation: MMA selection admits only tile shapes with a supported layout, and descriptor offsets follow that layout's concrete byte organization.
root_cause: MMA v3/v5 accepted N=8 without a valid no-swizzle descriptor and offset calculation.
physical_effect: The tensor-core instruction consumes wrong or invalid float16 operand bytes.
consequence: The reported H100 tests crash or mismatch about 98.2% of output elements, including NaNs.
repair: PR 7981 restricts default MMA v3/v5 selection to supported N and K tiles and introduces no-swizzle descriptor handling; PR 7986 corrects the remaining unswizzled right-hand-tile offset.
observed_decision: MMA v3/v5 accepted N=8 without a valid no-swizzle descriptor and offset calculation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 7981 restricts default MMA v3/v5 selection to supported N and K tiles and introduces no-swizzle descriptor handling; PR 7986 corrects the remaining unswizzled right-hand-tile offset.
review_note: The reporter identifies zero-swizzle handling, maintainers link both merged changes, and the reporter confirms the N=8 WGMMA test passes after those changes before separating a remaining XLA integration crash.

title: Incorrect results from `warp_specialize=True`
trigger: The consumer partition loads a shared-memory Y tile and then signals through arrive_barrier that the tile can be reused.
implemented_relation: A consumer reads the current shared-memory tile before publishing the barrier arrival that permits the producer to refill that storage.
validity_obligation: A memory read does not cross a write or synchronization side effect that changes when its storage may be modified.
root_cause: The reorder pass moved local_load across a write-side-effecting barrier operation.
physical_effect: Producer and consumer partitions race on the same shared-memory tile.
consequence: warp_specialize=True returns incorrect values for about 99.3% of the reported output elements.
repair: PR 8423 detects write side effects on the path between a local load and its proposed position and cancels the reorder when such an operation intervenes.
observed_decision: The reorder pass moved local_load across a write-side-effecting barrier operation.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8423 detects write side effects on the path between a local load and its proposed position and cancels the reorder when such an operation intervenes.
review_note: The issue shows the exact before/after IR swap and confirms that disabling the pass restores results; the merged patch blocks local-load movement across write side effects and adds that barrier pattern as a regression.

title: Multicta matmul miscompiles
trigger: A Blackwell matmul with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, four warps, and two CTAs lowers to tcgen05 two-CTA mode.
implemented_relation: The tensor-memory encoding maps register, lane, warp, and block coordinates from both CTAs to one logical accumulator tile.
validity_obligation: Every tensor-memory coordinate used to store or load a two-CTA MMA accumulator maps to the architecture-defined owner and logical output element.
root_cause: TensorMemoryEncodingAttr represented CTA splits without recording whether tcgen05 uses cta_group::2, so the M=64 layout followed the wrong conversion.
physical_effect: Accumulator fragments are written to or read from tensor-memory coordinates belonging to different logical output elements.
consequence: The two-CTA matmul mismatches 458,663 of 524,288 output elements, while the non-two-CTA BLOCK_N=128 control passes.
repair: PR 8644 adds an explicit twoCTAs attribute, constructs the special M=64 two-CTA layout, propagates and verifies the mode, and extends two-CTA matmul/layout tests.
observed_decision: TensorMemoryEncodingAttr represented CTA splits without recording whether tcgen05 uses cta_group::2, so the M=64 layout followed the wrong conversion.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 8644 adds an explicit twoCTAs attribute, constructs the special M=64 two-CTA layout, propagates and verifies the mode, and extends two-CTA matmul/layout tests.
review_note: The report isolates two-CTA lowering, and the linked patch states that the M=64 two-CTA layout was wrong and changes the corresponding tensor-memory coordinate bases and mode representation.

title: RAW hazard with pipelined wgmma and LHS in register
trigger: RAW hazard with pipelined wgmma and LHS in register
physical_effect: Pipelined WGMMA allows the next iteration's ldmatrix or register move to overwrite register-resident A fragments before all prior asynchronous matrix operations have consumed them.
consequence: The H100 kernel races fragment production with asynchronous consumption and produces large numerical corruption.
observed_decision: The pipeline emits wait_group N-1 while reusing A registers and relies on register moves/liveness scheduling that older ptxas versions may remove or place before the dependency barrier.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Triton PRs #9514/#9530 materialize moves in the correct position; CUDA 13.3 ptxas then staggers them around DEPBAR, and the reporter confirms the reproducer is fixed.
review_note: PRs 9514 and 9530 make the Triton PTX relation explicit and place moves before the fence, yet the report still observes a SASS hazard with ptxas 13.1 and attributes final success to ptxas 13.3. The ptxas repair is not archived, so the combined repair chain remains incomplete.

title: tl.store(i1, i32) implicitly casts int32 as int8 lead unexpected behavior
trigger: A bool reduction produces int32 value 256 and tl.store writes it to a bool output.
implemented_relation: A store to logical bool converts the source by value != 0 before representing the boolean in byte-addressable storage.
validity_obligation: Logical bool conversion precedes storage-width adaptation.
root_cause: TritonSemantic.store erased the bool destination identity before casting its source value.
physical_effect: The generated IR uses arith.trunci i32 to i8 and stores zero.
consequence: Summing 256 true values stores False.
repair: PR 11853 casts the value to int1 before adapting the bool pointer/value to int8 storage and adds an integer-to-bool frontend regression.
observed_decision: TritonSemantic.store erased the bool destination identity before casting its source value.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 11853 casts the value to int1 before adapting the bool pointer/value to int8 storage and adds an integer-to-bool frontend regression.
review_note: The issue's TTIR isolates truncation at store, and the merged patch names #9991 and changes precisely that cast order.

title: [Blackwell SM100] RuntimeError: misaligned address on tcgen05.mma
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises triton SM100 tensor-memory allocation for a two-dot kernel that promotes the left operand to tensor memory.
physical_effect: UTCHMMA executes with a misaligned tensor-memory operand.
consequence: The kernel raises CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS.
observed_decision: The allocation/layout path supplies tcgen05.mma with an address that violates its required alignment.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 10320 proposes disallowing the affected split-N 64-row layout; a downstream Helion workaround merged.
review_note: The Triton repair PR was not merged, and the downstream workaround does not correct Triton's allocator, so no landed upstream repair chain exists.

title: `make_tensor_descriptor` + `num_stages >= 3` produces `CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS`
trigger: A 16-byte tensor-descriptor load is software-pipelined with at least three stages.
implemented_relation: Each pipelined TMA transaction writes to the shared-memory slice assigned to its stage.
validity_obligation: Every stage destination selected for a TMA transaction satisfies the required shared-memory alignment.
root_cause: Descriptor-to-TMA selection checked the operation form but not whether the per-stage block size preserves alignment across the ring buffer.
physical_effect: A TMA transaction targets a misaligned shared-memory address.
consequence: Both reported kernels fail at runtime with CUDA_ERROR_MISALIGNED_ADDRESS when num_stages is three.
repair: PR 10898 checks the descriptor load block size against 128-byte alignment, excludes unaligned loads from TMA pipelining, lowers them through the pointer path, and adds runtime and IR regressions.
observed_decision: Descriptor-to-TMA selection checked the operation form but not whether the per-stage block size preserves alignment across the ring buffer.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 10898 checks the descriptor load block size against 128-byte alignment, excludes unaligned loads from TMA pipelining, lowers them through the pointer path, and adds runtime and IR regressions.
review_note: The reported failure begins only with multistaging, and the patch's alignment gate plus end-to-end test directly distinguish the unsafe TMA path from the repaired non-TMA path.

title: Probabilistic illegal memory access from a kernel with multiple tl.dot on H100 (sm_90)
trigger: Four dot operations execute in one sm_90 kernel across fresh processes with identical input shapes and launch parameters.
physical_effect: Some compiled-process instances perform an illegal GPU memory access although a load/store-identical reduction variant does not.
consequence: Approximately 40 to 60 percent of fresh H100 processes fail with cudaErrorIllegalAddress.
observed_decision: The report isolates the failure to the dot-containing compilation path but does not identify the responsible compiler transformation or generated invalid address.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Maintainers cannot reproduce on Triton main or GB200 and close the report as likely fixed.
review_note: No fixing commit, repaired transformation, before/after code contrast, or issue-specific regression is linked to the non-reproduction on main. The observed recovery therefore cannot support an implemented-relation-to-repair chain.

title: [BUG] sm_103 (B300): `tl.dot` chunked-recurrence kernel is non-deterministic with `num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}` — reproduces on Triton 3.7.0, i.e. NOT fixed by #9615 / #9871's fix
trigger: A grid larger than roughly one device wave runs recurrence kernels with four or eight warps and two or three pipeline stages.
physical_effect: Concurrent program instances observe nondeterministic recurrence state.
consequence: Repeated calls yield distinct outputs and can alter downstream expert routing during training.
observed_decision: The report suspects a missing fence or pipelining dependency but does not identify the transformed operation or generated ordering edge responsible on sm_103.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Two-warps configurations remain deterministic; the reporter confirms the full configuration matrix succeeds on Triton main.
review_note: Neither maintainers nor the reporter identify which main-branch commit fixed the behavior. Without the responsible source delta, generated-code contrast, and matching regression, the fixed-version run cannot establish the repair relationship.

title: [BUG][AMD] fp8 e4m3fnuz/e5m2fnuz NaN (byte 0x80) silently decodes to fp16/bf16 -0.0 instead of NaN on non-CDNA3 GPUs
trigger: The source byte is 0x80, the sole NaN encoding of an FNUZ FP8 format.
implemented_relation: The logical FNUZ NaN value remains NaN when its physical encoding changes to FP16 or BF16.
validity_obligation: The format-specific 0x80 case overrides generic zero and sign decoding in every software conversion path.
root_cause: Three software decoders either omitted the 0x80 case or applied it before later operations that clobbered the NaN result.
physical_effect: A special logical value silently becomes a finite value during representation conversion.
consequence: NaN propagation and masking observe -0.0 on non-CDNA3 AMD targets.
repair: PR 10747 places an explicit 0x80-to-NaN select after zero/sign decoding for e4m3fnuz and adds the missing e5m2fnuz and BF16 cases with conversion tests.
observed_decision: Three software decoders either omitted the 0x80 case or applied it before later operations that clobbered the NaN result.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 10747 places an explicit 0x80-to-NaN select after zero/sign decoding for e4m3fnuz and adds the missing e5m2fnuz and BF16 cases with conversion tests.
review_note: The issue enumerates the three decoders, and the merged patch adds explicit tests and guards for their exact 0x80 behavior.

title: [Bug] Two `tl.dot` chained through one accumulator in a K-loop compute wrong results on sm_103 (B300)
trigger: Two tcgen05 MMA operations update one logical accumulator in each K-loop iteration.
implemented_relation: MMA2 consumes MMA1's result in the same iteration, and MMA1 of the next iteration consumes the accumulator after MMA2 completes.
validity_obligation: Pipeline staging preserves every same-iteration and loop-carried accumulator dependency between chained MMA operations.
root_cause: AssignLatencies treated the chained MMAs as overlap candidates without detecting the accumulator's transfer cycle.
physical_effect: The next iteration reads an accumulator state that omits the second MMA from the preceding iteration.
consequence: Blackwell kernels show deterministic maximum absolute errors around 50 to 70, while single-MMA and separate-accumulator controls are correct.
repair: PR 10858 forwards chained MMAs to one accumulator where valid and detects loop-carried accumulator cycles so their MMA operations receive no movable latency; tests cover shared accumulators and cyclic transfers.
observed_decision: AssignLatencies treated the chained MMAs as overlap candidates without detecting the accumulator's transfer cycle.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 10858 forwards chained MMAs to one accumulator where valid and detects loop-carried accumulator cycles so their MMA operations receive no movable latency; tests cover shared accumulators and cyclic transfers.
review_note: The issue's controls isolate a shared accumulator on tcgen05, and the merged patch explicitly reconstructs that identity and blocks stage movement when its dependency graph crosses the loop boundary.

title: warpgroup_mma_wait does not properly synchronize across warpgroups
trigger: Eight warps share WGMMA operands and reuse shared memory after warpgroup_mma_wait(0).
implemented_relation: A nonlocal WGMMA wait makes completion and shared-memory liveness visible across every warpgroup participating in the CTA.
validity_obligation: A wait exposed as CTA-wide inserts cross-warpgroup synchronization when num_warps exceeds four.
root_cause: WarpGroupDotWaitOp did not represent whether its scope was local and lowering omitted a CTA barrier for multi-warpgroup use.
physical_effect: Warpgroups diverge around shared-memory reuse and read different B tiles.
consequence: The exact integer-valued matmul accumulation becomes intermittently incorrect.
repair: PR 11056 adds a warpGroupLocal attribute, emits nvvm.barrier after nonlocal waits when num_warps > 4, teaches membar analysis that such waits synchronize, and adds the reported two-warpgroup regression.
observed_decision: WarpGroupDotWaitOp did not represent whether its scope was local and lowering omitted a CTA barrier for multi-warpgroup use.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 11056 adds a warpGroupLocal attribute, emits nvvm.barrier after nonlocal waits when num_warps > 4, teaches membar analysis that such waits synchronize, and adds the reported two-warpgroup regression.
review_note: The re-applied patch explicitly fixes #11047 and adds the report's multi-warpgroup kernel plus LLVM barrier checks.

title: inline_asm_elementwise emits does not correctly handle replicated elements
trigger: The report's reproducer exercises triton inline_asm_elementwise lowering for impure assembly over layouts with replicated physical elements.
physical_effect: Replicated lanes perform duplicate writes to the same logical address.
consequence: Each output cell is incremented multiple times.
observed_decision: The lowering invokes side-effecting assembly once per physical replica instead of once per logical element.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 11089 proposes predicating replicated side effects.
review_note: PR 11089 was not merged, and the open discussion has no alternative landed semantics or regression.

title: triton seems to not lower a float8 e5m2 transposed store correctly in some conditions
trigger: A Triton kernel computes an FP8 value through NaN-propagating minimum/maximum and stores it through both contiguous and transposed vectorized layouts on Hopper with bundled ptxas 12.9.
implemented_relation: Both physical stores of one SSA value must preserve that value's bytes through register allocation and layout conversion.
validity_obligation: Backend register allocation and layout lowering preserve SSA value identity for every store layout and element type.
root_cause: The ptxas 12.9 compilation path assigns the transposed vectorized one-byte store a corrupted value under the min.NaN/max.NaN instruction shape.
physical_effect: Foreign bytes such as 0x60 or 0xFC reach the transposed output.
consequence: The transposed FP8 output contains NaN or Inf even though the identical contiguous output is finite; ptxas 13.3 does not reproduce it.
repair: TorchAO PR 4652 routes minimum/maximum through a numerically equivalent tl.where-based form before float8 compilation, avoiding min.NaN/max.NaN in the affected product path.
observed_decision: The ptxas 12.9 compilation path assigns the transposed vectorized one-byte store a corrupted value under the min.NaN/max.NaN instruction shape.
reported_repair_or_workaround: TorchAO PR 4652 routes minimum/maximum through a numerically equivalent tl.where-based form before float8 compilation, avoiding min.NaN/max.NaN in the affected product path.

title: [TritonGPU] OptimizeThreadLocality miscompiles loop accumulator with an additional in-loop use
trigger: A reduction loop stores the running accumulator inside the loop before updating it.
implemented_relation: Every in-loop use of the accumulator reads the logical running value carried by the original loop iteration argument.
validity_obligation: An accumulator rewrite preserves the running value observed by every in-loop consumer, not only the final yielded result.
root_cause: The collector checked uses of the reduction and update but did not reject an accumulator region argument with additional in-loop users.
physical_effect: Snapshot stores read zero instead of the accumulated values from prior iterations.
consequence: The snapshots are all zero instead of 0, 256, 512, and 768, although the final result is correct.
repair: PR 11842 requires the accumulator region iteration argument to have exactly one use before applying the rewrite and adds a negative test with an in-loop snapshot.
observed_decision: The collector checked uses of the reduction and update but did not reject an accumulator region argument with additional in-loop users.
reported_repair_or_workaround: PR 11842 requires the accumulator region iteration argument to have exactly one use before applying the rewrite and adds a negative test with an in-loop snapshot.
review_note: The issue and patch identify the same omitted use check; the one-line guard and negative regression preserve the path whose in-loop observation was miscompiled.

title: Pipelined dot-input load appears before gdc_wait and produces incorrect results with PDL
trigger: Pipelined dot-input load appears before gdc_wait and produces incorrect results with PDL
physical_effect: Software pipelining starts an asynchronous copy from producer-owned X before the programmatic-dependency wait has established that the producer finished writing X.
consequence: The consumer observes stale zero values and produces outputs with maximum absolute error 32 in all affected graph replays.
observed_decision: The pipeliner hoists the dependent loop load into the prologue across the side-effecting gdc_wait inside the loop.
reported_repair_or_workaround: Generated TTGIR and PTX place cp.async before griddepcontrol.wait; non-PDL, single-stage, and pre-loop-wait controls all produce the expected value while the affected configuration fails 20 of 20 replays.
review_note: The report localizes a load hoisted across gdc_wait, but the responsible source transformation, corrective patch, and fixed-version execution are unavailable.
